commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Export vllm:num_requests_kv_fetch_by_stage like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

vllm-project/vllm#58874 made the scheduler count waiting requests with an async KV load per load stage and send the counts in `SchedulerStats.num_kv_fetch_reqs_by_stage` (`waiting_to_start`, `in_progress`, `completed_waiting`). The Python frontend exports them as the gauge `vllm:num_requests_kv_fetch_by_stage{model_name, engine, stage}` and appends `KV fetch: <n> waiting to start, <n> in progress, <n> completed waiting` to the periodic stats log line when any count is non-zero. The Rust stats decoder ignores the field, so a P/D decode instance on the Rust frontend has neither the gauge nor the log segment. This PR decodes the field, exports the gauge, and adds the log segment.

## Claims

- `vllm:num_requests_kv_fetch_by_stage{model_name, engine, stage}` is exported with Python's help text, with one series per stage (`waiting_to_start`, `in_progress`, `completed_waiting`) per engine, at 0 from startup and updated on every scheduler-stats update.
- Absent stages, and the whole field from engines before vllm-project/vllm#58874, are treated as zero, like Python's `.get(stage, 0)`.
- The periodic stats log line gains the `KV fetch` segment after `Deferred`, when any count is non-zero, as in Python.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2320 tests run: 2320 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `protocol::stats::tests::scheduler_stats_kv_fetch_reqs_by_stage_defaults_and_decodes`: a MessagePack payload without the field decodes to zeros, and a sparse `{"waiting_to_start": 3, "in_progress": 1}` decodes to `[3, 1, 0]`.
- `metrics::tests::kv_fetch_reqs_by_stage_are_recorded_into_stage_gauges`: the three series exist at 0 from startup and take distinct per-stage values from a `SchedulerStats` update (snapshot).
- Red-green: with the recorder loop disabled, the second snapshot fails; on the base the family does not exist.
- The periodic log segment has no line test: the stats line is built inline in the logger loop with no formatting seam, and its `Deferred` and `Preemptions` segments have no line test either. The new segment reads the same gauges the recorder test pins.

## Details

- `SchedulerStats` decodes the field into a typed `KvFetchReqsByStage` (one `u64` per stage). Python sends a `dict[str, int]`; absent stages, and the whole field from engines before vllm-project/vllm#58874, default to zero, like Python's `.get(stage, 0)`.
- `vllm-metrics` registers `vllm:num_requests_kv_fetch_by_stage` with Python's help text and labels, and the scheduler-stats recorder sets one gauge per stage on every update, next to `vllm:num_requests_waiting_by_reason`.
- The periodic stats logger sums the stage gauges across engines and appends the `KV fetch` segment after `Deferred`, as Python does.

Ownership and layering: the wire field and its stage names live with `SchedulerStats` in `vllm-engine-core-client` (like `CachedTokensBySource`), the family in `vllm-metrics`, and recording in the existing per-engine handles, so the stats logger reads the same gauges it already reads for `Deferred`.

Divergence: Python registers the family only when `kv_transfer_config.is_kv_consumer`. The Rust frontend does not know the KV transfer role, so it pre-creates the three series for every engine, as it already does for the NIXL and Mooncake connector families; without a KV consumer they stay at 0. Making it exact would need the engine to report its KV role in the ready response.

Not a duplicate: no open PR exports `vllm:num_requests_kv_fetch_by_stage` from the Rust frontend.

commits.pr_body:
Raise `test_mrv2_weight_offloading` GPU memory utilization from 0.02 to 0.03 so XPU startup overhead does not exhaust the test budget before its offloader assertions. [Intel CI build 15605](https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/15605#01a17e53-adce-4b74-b35e-243d58a2eaec) fails on main (`eaf1627c01f5`) with `available_memory=-736133`; the same failure was seen in [build 15474](https://buildkite.com/vllm/intel-ci/builds/15474). The 0.02 setting was introduced by vllm-project/vllm#51440; that identifies its origin, not the first failing revision. No tests or assertions are skipped, and runtime defaults are unchanged.

This existing PR already addresses the exact build-15605 failure, so no duplicate PR was opened. Validation on Intel Arc Pro B60 with `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6,7 VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/basic_correctness/cpu_offload/test_cpu_offload.py -k test_mrv2_weight_offloading`: **2 passed, 6 deselected** on PR head `b5e17c41c977` (27.65s); both UVA and prefetch assertions ran. Current upstream baseline also passed locally (39.12s), so the CI failure was not reproduced here; UVA had only about 0.02 GiB KV headroom before, versus about 0.25 GiB with the fix. `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/basic_correctness/cpu_offload/test_cpu_offload.py` passed. Only targeted offload cases were run, not the full file; CUDA/ROCm were not available.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Build the folded q_b_proj / W_UK weight on the root model
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

#60110 folds `q_b_proj` and W_UK into one GEMM for Kimi-K3's MLA decode query on ROCm. The folded weight, `_w_fold`, is built in `KimiLinearForCausalLM.process_weights_after_loading`. But Kimi-K3 checkpoints load as `KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration`, and the model loader calls only the root model's `process_weights_after_loading`. The root model doesn't define one, so `_w_fold` stays `None`.

The fold is on whenever AITER MLA runs with an fp8 KV cache and no DCP / PCP. Every such serve then fails during startup, at the first CUDA graph capture (see the reproduction below). DCP > 1 is unaffected because the fold is off there.

This PR makes `KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration.process_weights_after_loading` call the text model's hook, which builds each MLA layer's `_w_fold`.

## Reproduction (`main` @ e96b490b12)

8× MI355X, `main`'s Python tree on image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-5d35ce39`, the newest nightly. The only `csrc` changes since that image are a perf-only ROCm int4 skinny-GEMM change and a CUDA-only NVFP4 MLA binding. vLLM's own decode path (no `decode_backend` override), TP8, DCP1, fp8 KV, DSpark k = 7, concurrency 1:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4BMM=1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm \
  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --language-model-only --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":16,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"],"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[8,16]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
```

On `main`, every TP rank fails about 3 minutes after launch, in the CUDA graph memory profile:

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 720, in determine_available_memory
    cudagraph_memory_estimate = self.model_runner.profile_cudagraph_memory()
...
File "vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mla.py", line 403, in forward
    attn_out = self._fused_decode(
File "vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mla.py", line 210, in _fused_decode
    assert self._w_fold is not None
AssertionError
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error '', please check the stack trace above for the root cause
```

## How this PR fixes it

`process_weights_after_loading` now runs on the text model, which calls `_build_w_fold()` on every MLA wrapper. `_fused_decode` therefore gets a real `_w_fold`. The fold's math is unchanged; only the missing call is added.

```python
def process_weights_after_loading(self) -> None:
    self.language_model.process_weights_after_loading()
```

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_qb_uk_fold.py`, which adds `test_root_model_builds_the_fold` (CPU-only, mocks the text model).
- The reproduction above, run on `main` and on this PR, then GSM8K 5-shot (all 1319 questions, `lm_eval` `local-completions`, concurrency 1, real rejection sampling).

## Test Result

| | `main` @ e96b490b12 | this PR (`main` + this commit) |
|---|---|---|
| `test_amd_qb_uk_fold.py` | new test fails, other 12 pass | 13 passed |
| Server startup (command above) | `AssertionError: self._w_fold is not None` at CUDA graph capture | ready in about 3.5 min, no tracebacks |
| GSM8K 5-shot, strict / flexible | — | **0.9659 / 0.9659** (±0.0050) |
| DSpark mean acceptance length | — | 4.62 |

For reference, #60683 reports GSM8K 0.9598 / 0.9629 (off / on) for Kimi-K3 at c1 k7, so this is within about one standard error.

The same commit is also in #61435. Whichever PR merges first, the other drops it on rebase.

commits.pr_title: [RL] Support per-update source ranks for NCCL weight transfer
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Support pipeline-parallel (partitioned) trainers in the dense NCCL weight-transfer backend. Each parameter is broadcast by its first `ParamMeta.owners` rank, as planned in #63256 (step 4). Single-sender behavior and wire format are unchanged.

## Claims

- A source whose ranks own different parameters (e.g. pipeline stages with `owners=(stage ranks...)`) is now accepted. Each stage's first owner broadcasts its own parameters to all inference workers within one start/finish lifecycle.
- No trainer-side coordination channel: every rank derives the same plan from `metadata`, which is identical on every rank. Broadcasters join the existing NCCL rendezvous at group ranks `[0, rank_offset)`, and rank 0 sends one `update_weights` per broadcaster, tagged with `src`.
- Workers receive each update from its `src`, which must be below `rank_offset`, and reuse metadata per `(model, src)`.
- Backward compatible: single-sender payloads are byte-identical to `main` (`rank_offset=1`, no `src` key), and a missing `src` defaults to 0.
- Invalid layouts are rejected at `trainer_init` on every rank before any NCCL call: a rank owning parameters of two broadcasters, unowned parameters with several broadcasters, or a `world_size` with no workers.

## Validation

4x A100, Qwen3-0.6B where a model is used.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py` (GPU) | 118 passed, 23 skipped (optional ModelExpress backend) |
| `test_nccl_weight_transfer_from_multiple_sources` (2 sources -> 2 workers, packed/unpacked, 2 rounds) | pass |
| `examples/rl/rlhf_nccl_multi_source.py` (2 stages -> TP2) | pass; setup 2.41s, iter 0 0.074s, iter 1 0.062s |
| `examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl.py` (single sender, `vllm serve`) | pass |
| `examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl_no_vllm.py` unpacked / `--packed` (raw HTTP trainer without `src`) | pass / pass |
| FSDP2 2-rank trainer -> TP2 (`rlhf_nccl_fsdp_ep.py` scaled to 4 GPUs), packed / unpacked | pass / pass |
| Cross-version: {PR, `main`} trainer x {PR, `main`} worker x {unpacked, packed}, 2 rounds | 8/8 pass |

Model evaluation is not applicable: this changes transport routing, not model output.

## Details

- Rank 0 is always group rank 0 and drives the control plane. Other broadcasters open their endpoints directly. Ranks that broadcast nothing stay out of the group and only drive `iter_full()` for their gathers.
- During each broadcaster's turn, the other broadcasters receive and discard its parameters to stay in the collective.
- Every parameter a rank owns must share its first owner, so that gathers and turns line up.
- A broadcaster failure during an update is fatal: that rank raises immediately, but peers can stay blocked in NCCL, so the job must be torn down. This is the same exposure as single-sender NCCL on `main`, and it is documented.
- No duplicate: #63256 explicitly leaves multi-sender NCCL to this PR.
- AI assistance was used. The human submitters reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

commits.pr_title: [Bench] Default to Zipf routing for forward benchmarks with dummy weights
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add `vllm bench forward --routing zipf` for skewed synthetic target-model MoE routing, with fixed alpha=1.25. The default `auto` selects Zipf with dummy weights and real routing otherwise; sequence-parallel TP ranks select their corresponding fixture token rows.

## Claims

- Each token selects distinct experts with weighted sampling without replacement; a seeded permutation assigns popularity ranks to expert IDs per layer.
- Reuse the existing gate-logit and explicit expert-ID hooks. Generate fixtures outside timing and keep them fixed across graph replays.
- Sequence-parallel ranks use their corresponding fixture slice instead of repeating rank zero's token rows.

## Validation

On GB200, with dummy weights:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Zipf frequency, distinct IDs, deterministic row prefixes | Passed |
| Existing Qwen3-Next hybrid CLI verification/mixed cases, default `auto` and explicit `balanced` | 2 passed; `auto` reports Zipf, override reports balanced; finite, deterministic graph outputs |
| Native DeepSeek V4.1 TP4/EP4 MegaMoE Q6/prefill | Correct fixture slices on all four ranks for both modes; finite outputs; Q6 graph/eager exact |

The native check uses a four-layer dummy DeepSeek V4.1 config (hidden size 512,
384 experts/top-6), `deep_gemm_mega_moe`, and cases `verify=6@1024:5` and
`prefill=1024`. Against the unmodified main routing module, ranks 1–3 reuse
rank zero's rows for both cases; the branch reconstructs the global fixture
exactly. For the first balanced Q6 layer this changes 12 distinct experts to
the intended 34. A separate real-TP-group check confirms replicated Q2 keeps
offset zero.

Native prefill output is not bitwise deterministic on either main or this
branch (eager-repeat relative RMS: 1.38% main, 1.42% balanced, 1.41% Zipf).
Those values are recorded as an existing limitation, not hidden by a relaxed
test tolerance. The fixture-row checks are exact.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py \
  -k 'zipf_expert_selection or bench_forward_hybrid_verify' -v
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/benchmarks/forward/routing.py vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py \
  tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py docs/benchmarking/cli.md \
  docs/cli/README.md .agents/skills/model-microbenchmark/SKILL.md
```

The existing Benchmarks CLI CI step selects both the sampler check and parameterized CLI test. Multi-GPU native MegaMoE validation is external to that single-GPU CI step. No serving code changes or model-quality claims: this option intentionally substitutes synthetic routing for benchmark inputs.

## Details

Exponential races implement weighted sampling without replacement with weights proportional to `rank**-1.25`. Chunked CPU generation bounds temporary memory. The expert-ID permutation avoids systematically assigning hot experts to the lowest EP ranks; load imbalance remains intentional. Seeding from global gate names keeps layer popularity stable across PP partitions.

The TP fix uses the native forward context's padded token count to recognize a local sequence shard. Replicated rows retain offset zero. Both synthetic modes share this correction. Grouped top-k remains unsupported; explicit Zipf also rejects prefill context parallelism, whose token mapping needs separate handling. When a synthetic fixture is unsupported, `auto` warns and falls back to real routing. Synthetic routing applies to the target, not the drafter.

Duplicate-work checks searched open PRs for `forward routing` and `zipf`. [#57100](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57100) is complementary: it changes only `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py` and uses a Gaussian-logit bias; it does not add full-model forward routing. [#63872](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63872) addresses Muse gate discovery/bias handling, not this new distribution. This branch is based directly on OSS main and does not bundle local timing experiments.

AI assistance was used to implement, validate, and review this change.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Export vllm:engine_sleep_state like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python exports `vllm:engine_sleep_state`, a per-engine gauge with one series per `sleep_state` label (`awake`, `weights_offloaded`, `discard_all`). `PrometheusStatLogger` creates it with the engines awake (`vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py:593-617`), and `AsyncLLM` updates it after each successful engine call (`vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py:1197-1217`, `record_sleep_state` at `loggers.py:1335-1352`). The Rust frontend routes `/sleep`, `/wake_up`, `/release_kv_cache_memory` and the gRPC sleep controls, but never exports this gauge, so `tests/entrypoints/rl/state_transitions/test_sleep.py::test_sleep_mode` fails under Rust only on its metric assertions. This PR registers the gauge and records the state after each successful sleep, wake-up and KV-cache release call.

## Claims

- `vllm:engine_sleep_state{model_name, engine, sleep_state}` is exported per engine with Python's help text, and starts with `awake` at 1.
- The series follow Python's transitions: `sleep(level=1)` sets `weights_offloaded`, `sleep(level=2)` sets `discard_all`, `sleep(level=0)` and `release_kv_cache_memory()` set all three to 0, and a `wake_up` that returns fully awake sets `awake` back to 1. A `wake_up` with only part of the engine awake leaves the state unchanged.
- The gRPC `Sleep` call rejects an unknown level with `InvalidArgument` instead of forwarding it to the engine; the HTTP route already rejected it.
- With `--disable-log-stats` nothing is recorded, as in Python.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2320 tests run: 2320 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `sleep_and_wake_calls_record_engine_sleep_state` (`vllm-engine-core-client`) drives a client against two scripted engines through `sleep(1)`, a partial `wake_up(["weights"])` where only engine 1 reports fully awake, a full `wake_up`, `release_kv_cache_memory`, and `sleep(2)`. It snapshots the rendered series of both engines after each step, and the snapshot matches the table in Details. It fails with the three record calls removed, and on the base, where all series are missing.
- `control_sleep_rejects_unknown_level`: the gRPC `Sleep` call returns `InvalidArgument` for an unknown level.

## Details

Python behavior (`vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py`, `vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py`):

| Call | `awake` | `weights_offloaded` | `discard_all` |
|---|---|---|---|
| startup | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| `sleep(level=1)` | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| `sleep(level=2)` | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| `sleep(level=0)` or `release_kv_cache_memory()` | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `wake_up(tags)` returning fully awake | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| `wake_up(tags)` with only part of the engine awake | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged |

Changes:

- `vllm-metrics`: register `vllm:engine_sleep_state` with Python's help text and the labels `model_name`, `engine` and `sleep_state`.
- `vllm-engine-core-client`: `SchedulerStatsRecorder` resolves the three series per engine and sets the engines awake when it is created. `EngineCoreClient::sleep`, `release_kv_cache_memory` and `wake_up` record the new state after the utility call succeeds. A partial wake-up leaves the state unchanged.
- `SleepLevel` (`PauseOnly`, `OffloadWeights`, `DiscardAll`) in `protocol::utility`, serialized as Python's integer level. The HTTP query and the gRPC request lower into it, `EngineCoreClient::sleep` takes it, and the gauge mapping is an exhaustive `match`. `release_kv_cache_memory` gets its own `KvCacheReleased` state.

**Ownership and layering.** In Python, the state is recorded by the engine client (`AsyncLLM`), not by the HTTP route. The Rust counterpart is `EngineCoreClient`, which both the HTTP routes and the gRPC control service call, so the gauge covers both entry points. The handles live in `SchedulerStatsRecorder`, which already holds the per-engine, engine-labeled stat-logger series and exists only when engines record stats. This matches Python, where `--disable-log-stats` leaves `logger_manager` unset and nothing is recorded.

`tests/entrypoints/rl/state_transitions/test_sleep.py::test_sleep_mode` expects the metric behavior added here; the sleep, wake and tag routes themselves already pass under Rust.

Not a duplicate: no open PR exports `vllm:engine_sleep_state` from the Rust frontend. vllm-project/vllm#59130 redesigns sleep-state telemetry into new per-resource series and keeps this gauge; it has had no activity since 2026-10-10.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Return 404 for a missing LoRA adapter path like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`POST /v1/load_lora_adapter` with a local path that does not exist returns 404 `NotFoundError` on the Python frontend: the engine's worker manager raises `LoRAAdapterNotFoundError` on `FileNotFoundError`, and `create_error_response` maps every `VLLMNotFoundError` to 404 (vllm-project/vllm#11727 added the check and `test_dynamic_lora_not_found`). The Rust frontend answers the same request with 400 `"Local LoRA adapter path must exist and be accessible."`, because its runtime path guard (`validate_lora_path_access`, vllm-project/vllm#43778 and vllm-project/vllm#53756) folds every `canonicalize` failure into one `InvalidPath` error. A client that tells "no such adapter" from "bad request" by status code, and `tests/entrypoints/serve/lora/test_lora_adapters.py::test_dynamic_lora_not_found` (which expects `openai.NotFoundError`), see a different answer. This PR makes the guard distinguish a missing path and maps it to 404.

## Claims

- A local adapter path that does not exist returns 404 `NotFoundError` with `param: null` and the message `No adapter found for <path>` (the tail of Python's `Loading lora <name> failed: No adapter found for <path>`), like Python.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Count gpt-oss reasoning tokens like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

For gpt-oss, the Rust frontend always reports `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens: 0`, even when the response has `reasoning` content. Python counts them since vllm-project/vllm#58626: `HarmonyParser._is_reasoning_token` counts a generated token when the Harmony parser places it in an `analysis` message, or in a `commentary` message with a recipient (a tool call), and it is not a Harmony control token (`<|channel|>`, `<|message|>`, `<|end|>`, ...). Chat Completions and Responses share that rule. The native Harmony output processor (`rust/src/chat/src/output/harmony/mod.rs`) never measured reasoning tokens: every reasoning delta carried `token_count: None` (with a TODO), and the final usage was built with `finished.usage.into()`, which sets `reasoning_tokens: 0`. This PR applies Python's rule in the processor.

## Claims

- The final `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` for gpt-oss matches Python: tokens in `analysis` messages and in `commentary` messages with a recipient are counted; `final` content, commentary preambles without a recipient, header tokens and Harmony control tokens are not.
- Each reasoning text delta carries the tokens of its own text as `token_count`, so `stream_options.continuous_usage_stats` reports reasoning tokens as they stream, like the unified parsers. A token whose content delta is still empty (a split UTF-8 character) is attributed to the next delta of the same message.
- Tool-call tokens, which Python also counts as reasoning, have no text delta to carry them, so they reach the client only through the final usage.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2322 tests run: 2322 passed, 13 skipped
```

New tests in `output/harmony/tests.rs`, ported from Python's `TestCountReasoningTokens` (`tests/parser/test_harmony.py`):

- `reasoning_tokens_count_analysis_and_tool_call_content`: analysis text plus a `commentary to=functions.get_weather` call counts both bodies' content tokens, without header or control tokens; the deltas carry the analysis tokens only.
- `reasoning_tokens_exclude_final_and_preamble_content`: a commentary preamble without a recipient and a final message count 0.
- `reasoning_tokens_are_attributed_to_their_streamed_deltas`: one token per decoded update across two analysis messages; each delta carries exactly one token, the separating newline none, and the final count equals the analysis content tokens.
- `reasoning_tokens_of_a_split_character_join_its_delta`: characters that span several byte-level tokens; the tokens that produce no text yet are counted on the delta that completes the character.
- `interrupted_analysis_message_is_preserved` now expects `reasoning_tokens: 1` instead of 0.

Red-green: with the fix reverted, the three positive counting tests and the updated `interrupted_analysis_message_is_preserved` fail; the exclusion test passes on both, as a negative guard.

## Details

- `HarmonyState` applies Python's rule to each token right after the Harmony parser consumes it. Header tokens are not counted, because the oss-harmony parser reports a channel only once the header is complete (in `StreamState::Content`), and control tokens are excluded with the encoding's `is_special_token`.
- The total goes into `ChatTokenUsage::reasoning_tokens` on `Done`, so the final `usage` matches Python.
- Each reasoning text delta carries the tokens of its own text as `token_count`, which feeds continuous usage like the unified parsers do.

**Ownership and layering.** The Harmony output processor in `vllm-chat` is the only Rust consumer of the generated Harmony token IDs (it drives `StreamableParser` over them), so it is the one place that knows each token's channel and recipient. It reports the count through the existing `token_count` and `ChatTokenUsage` path that the server already turns into `completion_tokens_details`; nothing in `vllm-server` changes.

**Known gap.** Tool-call tokens reach continuous usage only at `Done`, while Python counts them as the call streams. No text delta carries them, and widening the tool-call events for a usage counter is out of scope here.

**Scope.** This PR only counts. Whether `completion_tokens_details` is serialized at all when no reasoning parser is configured is a separate change.

Python reference: vllm-project/vllm#58626 (`HarmonyParser.count_reasoning_tokens`, `_is_reasoning_token`).

Not a duplicate: no open PR counts gpt-oss reasoning tokens in the Rust frontend.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept list-form chat templates like Transformers
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`tokenizer_config.json` may store `chat_template` as a list of named templates instead of a string. `NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B` ships `[{"name": "default", ...}, {"name": "tool_use", ...}]`. On Python, Transformers collects the list into a dict when it loads the tokenizer, and vLLM resolves the template per request through `tokenizer.get_chat_template(chat_template, tools=tools)` (`vllm/renderers/hf.py` `resolve_chat_template`): with tools it uses `tool_use` if present, otherwise `default`. On Rust, `HfTokenizerConfig.chat_template` is `Option<String>`, so parsing `tokenizer_config.json` fails and the frontend does not start for such models. This PR parses both forms and selects the named template per request like Transformers.

## Claims

- A model whose `tokenizer_config.json` stores `chat_template` as a list of named templates loads on the Rust frontend.
- Requests with tools render with the `tool_use` template when present; requests without tools render with `default`.
- For `NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B`, the Rust renderer's prompts match Transformers byte for byte, with and without tools.
- A configured `--chat-template`, a dedicated template file, and a request-level `chat_template` override keep their precedence over tokenizer-config templates.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2320 tests run: 2320 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `vllm-chat` `backend::hf::tests::hf_renderer_selects_named_tokenizer_config_templates_like_transformers` loads a list-form `tokenizer_config.json` through the backend. It renders `default` without tools and `tool_use` with tools. It also checks, with a tool request, that a configured `--chat-template` and a dedicated `chat_template.jinja` replace both named templates.
  - Without the fix it fails in model-file loading with "invalid type: sequence, expected a string".
  - Without the two lines that clear `tool_use_template` on override, it fails as well (red-green checked).
- `vllm-text` `tokenizer_config_reads_single_and_named_chat_templates` covers single templates, duplicate names, and a list without `default`.
- Real checkpoint: with the actual `NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B` `config.json` and `tokenizer_config.json`, the Rust renderer's prompts match `transformers` 5.20.2 `apply_chat_template` byte for byte, both without tools and with a `get_weather` tool.

## Details

- `vllm-text` parses `chat_template` as `HfChatTemplate::{Single, Named}`, the owner of the `tokenizer_config.json` schema. It exposes the two names Transformers selects on its own: `default_template()` and `tool_use_template()`. A later list entry wins over an earlier one with the same name, as in Transformers' dict.
- `HfChatRenderer` compiles the `tool_use` template next to the default one and picks it when the request has tools (`request.tools()`, the same tools it passes to the template). Other requests use the default. A configured `--chat-template` or a dedicated template file still replaces every tokenizer-config template, `tool_use` included, as before. A request-level `chat_template` override still wins.

**Ownership and layering.** The schema and Transformers' naming convention live where `tokenizer_config.json` is parsed (`vllm-text`). The per-request choice lives in the HF renderer, the only consumer that compiles and renders the template. Each named template is compiled once at load, and its content format is detected separately, as Python does for the template it resolves.

**Not covered.**

- Python also resolves a request `chat_template` (with `--trust-request-chat-template`) that names one of the model's templates. Rust compiles the string as a literal template, as it already did.
- Transformers' `additional_chat_templates/` directory is not read either; dedicated-file discovery is unchanged.
- `/tokenize` with an explicit `tools: []`: Python passes `[]` to Transformers, which selects `tool_use`. Rust lowers omitted and empty tools to the same empty vector, so it selects `default`. This only affects `/tokenize`; chat completions and render reject `tools: []` with 400, as Python does. The same lost presence already makes Rust pass no `tools` variable where Python passes `[]`, independent of this PR. Fixing it means carrying tool presence through `ResolvedToolContext`, which is a separate change.

Python reference: Transformers `PreTrainedTokenizerBase.get_chat_template` and `vllm/renderers/hf.py` `resolve_chat_template`.

Not a duplicate: no open PR accepts list-form `chat_template` in the Rust frontend.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Reject max_tokens above max_model_len like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Python's chat and completions reject an output budget larger than the whole context window. `build_tok_params` passes the request's budget and `max_model_len` to `TokenizeParams`, whose `__post_init__` (`vllm/renderers/params.py`) raises a 400 before rendering: "`max_tokens=N cannot be greater than max_model_len=M. Please request fewer output tokens.`", with `param` naming the field (`max_completion_tokens` when the chat request sets it, otherwise `max_tokens`). A budget that fits the window is then clamped to the room the prompt leaves by `get_max_tokens()`. The Rust frontend only clamps: `vllm_text::resolve_max_tokens` takes the minimum of the requested budget and `max_model_len - prompt_len`, so `max_tokens=100000` against a 4096-token window succeeds and generates up to the window instead of returning 400. This PR adds the rejection to the chat and completions handlers and their render handlers.

## Claims

- Chat and completions requests whose output budget is above `max_model_len` return 400, as do their render requests; `param` names `max_completion_tokens` or `max_tokens`.
- A budget within `max_model_len` but above the room the prompt leaves is still clamped and returns 200.
- `/inference/v1/generate` is unchanged and still clamps any budget.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2321 tests run: 2321 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `chat_and_completions_reject_max_tokens_above_max_model_len` (serve app over the mock engine, whose `max_model_len` is 1048576; budget one above it): chat `max_tokens`, chat `max_completion_tokens`, and completions `max_tokens` each return the 400 above; snapshot of the three error bodies.
- `render_rejects_max_tokens_above_max_model_len` (render server, `max_model_len=64`): chat and completions render return the same 400 for 65, and completions render accepts `max_tokens=64`.
- Both tests fail with the handler checks reverted (200 instead of 400). The serve test runs against a mock engine that answers, so a submitted request fails the assertion instead of hanging.
- `resolve_max_tokens_caps_budget_above_model_len` (`vllm-text`) pins that shared lowering still only clamps a budget above the window, which `/inference/v1/generate` relies on. It fails if the rejection moves into shared lowering; a generate route test would need a scripted engine for the same assertion.

## Details

| Request | Python | Rust before | Rust after |
|---|---|---|---|
| chat or completions, budget > `max_model_len` | 400 | 200, clamped | 400 |
| chat or completions, `max_model_len - prompt_len` < budget ≤ `max_model_len` | 200, clamped | 200, clamped | 200, clamped |
| chat or completions render, budget > `max_model_len` | 400 | 200 | 400 |
| `/inference/v1/generate`, any budget | 200, clamped | 200, clamped | 200, clamped |

**Ownership and layering.** The rejection is protocol policy, not a property of the shared lowering: Python's generate route builds `TokenizeParams(max_total_tokens=None)` and only clamps, and Rust's generate route lowers through the same `vllm_text::lower_sampling_params`, so putting the check in `resolve_max_tokens` would wrongly reject generate requests. The check is a small shared helper in `routes/openai/utils` (`validate_max_output_tokens`) called by the chat and completions handlers and their render handlers on the lowered request's `max_tokens`, right after `prepare_*`/`lower_*` (so the model-not-found and other compat checks still come first, as in Python). Those handlers are where `max_model_len` is known (the engine's value on serve, the configured value on the render server, unlimited when unset); passing it into `prepare_*` instead would touch about 70 test call sites.

**Deviations.**

- Rust normalizes the deprecated chat `max_tokens` into `max_completion_tokens` when the request is parsed, so a chat request that sends only `max_tokens` is reported with `param` and message `max_completion_tokens`, where Python says `max_tokens`. The status code and the budget/limit values match.
- Python's final message carries `VLLMValidationError`'s ` (parameter=max_tokens, value=65)` suffix and Rust's does not. Rust error messages omit that suffix throughout and carry the field in `param`, so this is the same wording difference as for every other ported validation.

Python reference: the check came with `TokenizeParams` in vllm-project/vllm#32863; vllm-project/vllm#57035 later stopped subtracting the output budget from the prompt budget, which left this check as the only rejection of a large budget. No Python test pins the message.

Overlaps vllm-project/vllm#63649, which adds the same check to the chat and completions routes (not the render routes). The closed vllm-project/vllm#58711 rejected a different case (a budget above the room the prompt leaves, which both frontends clamp since vllm-project/vllm#57035) and did it in the shared `resolve_max_tokens`, which also rejected generate requests.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Reject non-linear expert placement with EP
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #62801.

Reject non-linear expert placement when wrapping fused MoE layers with LoRA and expert parallelism. Adapter loading slices a contiguous range of global experts per EP rank, which does not match round-robin ownership.

## Claims

- Check the MoE runner's resolved placement and raise a `ValueError` naming the incompatible strategy before adapter weights are allocated.
- Preserve linear placement, including requested round-robin placement that resolves to linear, and configurations without EP.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/lora/test_moe_lora_ep_load.py tests/distributed/test_expert_placement.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py tests/lora/test_moe_lora_ep_load.py
```

- 12 tests passed. The added regression fails on unmodified main: 1 failed, 4 passed. It uses `ExpertMapManager` to exercise actual placement resolution, including the linear fallback.
- Changed-file pre-commit passed, including mypy.
- Real two-process XPU EP validation: a tiny randomly initialized DeepSeek-V2 fixture with two expert groups starts with round-robin on main; both workers reject it with the new error after this change.
- Tiny Qwen3-MoE FP16, TP2+EP, eager, `allgather_reducescatter`: linear and requested round-robin resolving to linear both completed base → nonzero expert adapter → base generation (two prompts, eight output tokens each). Token IDs and logprobs matched unmodified-main linear results exactly across all three phases (maximum logprob difference 0.0); both workers confirmed nonzero expert adapter weights.
- All-files pre-commit was run. It regenerated an unrelated ROCm dependency lockfile, and the entrypoint test failed under root. All 11 entrypoint cases passed as a non-root user; generated lock changes are excluded. Type checking reported no errors; the final changed-file run passed.

The existing Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.13 XPU / Triton 3.7 environment was preserved; main pins PyTorch 2.14. The model fixtures validate distributed startup and generation behavior, not trained-model quality. CUDA/ROCm hardware validation was not run.

## Details

`MoERunner.expert_placement_strategy` forwards the resolved expert-map strategy. Checking the requested parallel configuration would incorrectly reject valid fallback-to-linear configurations. The check runs once during wrapper initialization.

For example, with four experts and EP2, round-robin rank 0 owns experts 0 and 2, while the contiguous LoRA checkpoint filter selects experts 0 and 1.

Duplicate-work checks found no PR implementing this placement guard. Related open work [#49058](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49058) addresses SP restrictions and padded LoRA buffers; [#48460](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48460) handles partial fused MoE adapters. Their diffs do not validate resolved expert placement.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Use server-reported prompt_tokens in vllm-bench
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59576. Port #38654 to the Rust `vllm-bench`.

Python `vllm bench serve` takes each request's input length from the server's `usage.prompt_tokens`. The Rust bench still used the client-side estimate:

- `ChunkUsage` only deserialized `completion_tokens`, so the `openai` and `openai-chat` backends dropped `prompt_tokens`; `ResponsesUsage` likewise dropped `input_tokens` in `openai-responses`.
- `calculate_metrics` and the steady-state window summed `input_requests[i].prompt_len` (the client estimate) instead of `outputs[i].prompt_len`.

As a result, Total input tokens and input/total token throughput were under-reported whenever the server counted more tokens than the client estimate: chat-template tokens and, most visibly, multimodal tokens in `random-mm` / VLM benchmarks. Rust and Python results for the same server didn't match.

This PR:
- adds `prompt_tokens` to `ChunkUsage` and a `ChunkUsage::apply` helper that both streaming backends (`openai`, `openai-chat`) call, so the usage rule lives in one place;
- reads `usage.input_tokens` from the `response.completed` / `response.incomplete` event in `openai-responses`, as Python's `async_request_openai_responses` does;
- sums `output.prompt_len` in `calculate_metrics` and the steady-state window, as Python's `serve.py` does, and removes the now-unused `input_requests` parameter from both, together with the `Vec<SampleRequest>`s that `calculate_multi_turn_metrics` built only to pass it in;
- renames the dry-run line to "Estimated total input tokens", since it still sums the client estimate and will no longer match real runs (most visibly for multimodal);
- updates the stale `steady_state::compute` and `calculate_embedding_metrics` docs.

If the server omits the count, or reports `0` (some OpenAI-compatible servers send placeholder zeros in usage chunks), `output.prompt_len` keeps the client-side estimate it is initialized with.

### Behavior change: multi-turn

Multi-turn total and per-turn input now come from each turn's server-reported `prompt_tokens`, which include chat-template and image tokens, so they are higher than before for chat and multimodal datasets. #51109 (merged) already switched these totals to `request_output.prompt_len`; this PR makes that value the server count. The `max_model_len` pre-filter in `multi_turn.rs` still uses the client estimate, since it runs before any request is sent.

## Not a duplicate

I checked open PRs that touch `rust/src/bench/src/backends/` or `rust/src/bench/src/metrics/`:

- #55809 adds server queue time / TTFT to the detailed results. Different change; it touches the same backend files, so a textual conflict is possible but no overlap in behavior.
- #51109 (multi-turn input-token accounting) is merged; this branch is synced with `main` and keeps its multi-turn test.
- #60177 rewrites the chat SSE test helper; the new completions test uses its own small helper to avoid touching that.

## Test Plan

New tests:
- `openai_chat::tests::test_usage_prompt_tokens_override_prompt_len`: the server reports `prompt_tokens = 128` against a client estimate of 100, so `output.prompt_len == 128`.
- `openai_chat::tests::test_missing_prompt_tokens_keeps_client_prompt_len`: the server omits `prompt_tokens`, so `output.prompt_len` stays 100 and `output_tokens` is still 3.
- `openai_completions::tests::test_usage_prompt_tokens_override_prompt_len`: same as the chat test, for `/v1/completions`.
- `openai_responses::tests::test_terminal_usage_input_tokens_override_prompt_len`: `input_tokens = 128` in `response.completed` sets `prompt_len == 128`.
- `backends::tests::chunk_usage_ignores_zero_prompt_tokens`: `prompt_tokens = 0` keeps the client estimate.
- `calculator::tests::test_total_input_uses_output_prompt_len`: outputs reporting 128 give `total_input == 256`.

Multi-turn is covered by `calculator::tests::test_multi_turn_metrics_use_request_prompt_lengths` from #51109. In the steady-state tests, outputs are now the only source of input lengths (`mk_full` sets `prompt_len: 10`, and `compute_constant_concurrency_matches_full_run` checks `input_throughput`).

Commands:
```bash
cargo test -p vllm-bench --lib
cargo clippy -p vllm-bench --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

End-to-end: a mock OpenAI-compatible server that reports `usage.prompt_tokens = 128` for every request, `--dataset-name random --random-input-len 100 --random-output-len 8 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 8`, run against both the `openai-chat` (`/v1/chat/completions`) and `openai` (`/v1/completions`) backends, compared with Python `vllm bench serve`.

## Test Result

- `cargo test -p vllm-bench --lib`: 204 passed. Clippy `-D warnings` and fmt are clean.
- With the usage handling reverted, the chat backend test fails as expected (`left: 100, right: 128`).

End-to-end, Total input tokens:

|---|---|---|
| Python `vllm bench serve` | 4096 | 4096 |
| Rust `vllm-bench`, before | 3185 | 3185 |
| Rust `vllm-bench`, after | 4096 | 4096 |

`openai-responses` is covered by the unit test above; the mock server doesn't implement `/v1/responses`.

commits.pr_title: [MRV2][Spec Decode] Close DFlash/DSpark and adaptive-verification JIT warmup gaps
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Three Triton kernels on the MRV2 spec-decode path still JIT-compile during serving after warmup, triggering `Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: ...` from the JIT monitor and a latency spike on that step (and a hard failure under `--jit-monitor-mode=error`). Seen while serving Muse-Spark-Open with a DSpark drafter; reproduced on small models.

## Claims

- `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` (DFlash/DSpark) compiles once instead of once per power-of-two prefill chunk bucket; decode-time kernel GPU time drops ~3x as a side effect.
- `_accumulate_kernel` (adaptive verification acceptance estimator) compiles once for all batch sizes.
- `_refit_kernel` is compiled at warmup instead of 100 steps into serving.
- No output changes: `prepare_dflash_inputs` outputs are bitwise identical; estimator statistics differ only by fp32 summation order.

## Validation

**End to end, `jit_monitor_verbose=True`, MRV2, B300** (repro script runs a battery of batch sizes / prompt lengths after warmup):

| Config | Runtime JIT before | Runtime JIT after |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-4B + `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dspark`, k=7, prompts 5–3000 tokens | `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` `BLOCK_SIZE=128`, `BLOCK_SIZE=256` | none |
| Qwen3-8B + `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16`, k=7, `enable_adaptive_verification`, `max_num_seqs=1024`, bs 1/200/300/600/1000, >100 steps | `_refit_kernel`, `_accumulate_kernel` `BLOCK_R=512` (bs=300) | none from these kernels |

<details>
<summary>Repro script</summary>

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(
    "Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
    speculative_config={"method": "dflash", "model": "z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16",
                        "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic",
                        "rejection_sample_method": "block",
                        "enable_adaptive_verification": True},
    jit_monitor_verbose=True, max_model_len=4096, max_num_seqs=1024,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.6,
)
for bs, max_tokens in ((1, 600), (200, 64), (300, 64), (600, 64), (1000, 64)):
    prompts = [{"prompt_token_ids": list(range(1000 + i, 1040 + i))} for i in range(bs)]
    llm.generate(prompts, SamplingParams(max_tokens=max_tokens, temperature=0.8,
                                         ignore_eos=True), use_tqdm=False)
```
Run with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. The DSpark variant swaps in the DSpark model pair and varies prompt length.
</details>

**Kernel GPU time, `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`** (CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2, B300; k=7, sample-from-anchor, block-table stride 4096). All block-size policies produce bitwise-identical outputs on every case.

| max reqs / tokens | case | before (dynamic) | fixed 128 (this PR) | fixed 256 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 / 8192 | decode bs1 | 19.7 us | 7.5 | 7.8 |
| 256 / 8192 | decode bs256 | 14.3 | 5.3 | 5.6 |
| 256 / 8192 | mixed 1x2048 + 63 decode | 6.8 | 6.3 | 6.8 |
| 256 / 8192 | prefill 1x8192 | 8.0 | 7.7 | 7.9 |
| 1024 / 16384 | decode bs1 | 38.1 | 12.5 | 12.6 |
| 1024 / 16384 | decode bs256 | 33.4 | 9.6 | 10.1 |
| 1024 / 16384 | mixed 1x2048 + 63 decode | 11.2 | 10.8 | 11.3 |
| 1024 / 16384 | prefill 1x8192 | 13.0 | 13.1 | 12.9 |

Fixed 512 was slower on every row. 128 vs 256 is within ~0.5 us.

**Kernel GPU time, `_accumulate_kernel`** (k=7, `max_num_reqs=1024`): pinning `BLOCK_R=1024, num_warps=4` is within run-to-run noise (~±0.5 us on a ~4 us kernel) of the old per-batch sizing for bs 1–1024; max relative difference in the accumulated statistics is 1.6e-7. A tiled loop over a fixed 256-wide block was also tried and rejected: up to 2x slower at bs 1024.

**Tests**

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_acceptance_estimator.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py -q
# 14 passed
```

The two new compile-count tests fail on `main` and pass with this PR. `test_warmup_covers_every_batch_size_and_the_refit` also fails when only the `BLOCK_R` fix is reverted.

No model evals: the DFlash prep outputs are bitwise identical, and the estimator change only reorders an fp32 reduction.

## Details

**Root cause.** Each kernel had a `tl.constexpr` derived from the live batch, and warmup only reaches a few of its values:

- `prepare_dflash_inputs` set `BLOCK_SIZE = min(256, next_power_of_2(max_query_len + num_query_per_req))`. Warmup prefill/decode steps are tiny, so 128/256 (and, depending on config, smaller buckets) first compile on a real prefill chunk. A fixed `BLOCK_SIZE` with a variable `num_blocks` grid covers every span with one variant. It also fixes a perf cliff: the padding loops at the end of the kernel stride by `BLOCK_SIZE`, so at decode (`BLOCK_SIZE` 8/16) they walked `max_num_tokens` in 8- or 16-element steps.
- `_accumulate_kernel` used `BLOCK_R = max(256, next_power_of_2(num_reqs))`. Warmup reaches 256 and `max_num_seqs`, not the buckets in between. `BLOCK_R` is now computed once from `max_num_reqs`.
- `_refit_kernel` runs every `REFIT_INTERVAL` (100) steps. `OnlineAcceptanceEstimator.warmup()`, called at the end of `warmup_kernels`, clears the per-round statistics and runs a refit. With zero statistics the Newton step is exactly zero, so the coefficients don't move. This also stops dummy warmup observations from leaking into the first real refit round, which is a small behavior change.

**Scope.** The estimator is only active with adaptive verification and a drafter without a confidence head (e.g. DFlash). DSpark checkpoints with `enable_confidence_head` disable it.

**Related PRs.**
- #58559 also targets `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`, by explicitly launching every `BLOCK_SIZE` bucket at warmup. This PR removes the variant set instead: one compile, no warmup code, and faster decode. #58559 has merge conflicts and no review activity since September. Its DSv4 top-k part is unrelated to this PR.
- #58633 gives the padding loops a separate `PAD_BLOCK_SIZE`. It overlaps with the decode speedup here, and its `min(1024, next_power_of_2(pad_span))` sizing varies with batch size, so it could reintroduce runtime compiles.
- #56323 / #56654 added, then reverted, explicit JIT warmup for these MRV2 kernels.

**Known remaining gap, not addressed here.** `_gumbel_sample_kernel` (main sampler, `APPLY_TEMPERATURE=False, IS_DRAFTING=False`) still JITs on the first request that takes the non-fused sampling path: no top-k/top-p, or explicit seed, or processed logprobs. Warmup's sampled pass uses top-k/top-p, so it takes the fused FlashInfer sampler path, and its other pass is greedy.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Pad staged prefill KV to avoid a trtllm-gen out-of-bounds read
commits.pr_body:
## Problem

HiSparse prefill randomly crashes with `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` in `sparse_mla_attention.forward_mqa` → `_forward_mqa_kernel` on the staged prefill cache. `HiSparseRuntime.gather_prefill_cache` stages a request's KV into an exact-size buffer (often 1–3 blocks of 64 rows), and FlashInfer's trtllm-gen sparse MLA decode kernel reads ~170–250 rows from the start of its KV cache regardless of the cache's size or the top-k indices (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6484). It faults whenever the caching allocator puts the staged buffer near an unmapped page. Surfaced in #61487 (HiSparse + DBO); DBO makes it more frequent but it is not DBO-specific.

## Fix

Allocate at least 256 rows behind the staged buffer and return the exact-size view, so all downstream shapes are unchanged. Cost: ≤168 KB of transient allocation per staged layer.

## Test plan

Hardware: 2x B200 (pirate2 dell-b200-01), flashinfer 0.7.0.post1, torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0. vLLM `2f18d13cf` with and without this PR's diff.

**Kernel.** The flashinfer#6484 repro places an FP8 KV cache so it ends at an unmapped 2 MiB page. It faults with 1–3 pages (64–192 rows) and is clean with 4, 5, 6, 8 and 16 pages, at batch sizes 1–128. Bisecting the slack shows the kernel reads about 170–227 rows from the start of the cache, under the 256-row floor.

**Server.** GLM-5.3 NVFP4 with dummy weights and 8 layers, DP2 + EP, eager. Each server takes 3 rounds of 128 concurrent 30-word completions with `max_tokens=128`.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 8}' \
  -tp 1 -dp 2 --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend deepep_low_latency \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":24}}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}'
# The DBO rows add: --enable-dbo --dbo-decode-token-threshold 2 --dbo-prefill-token-threshold 512
```

| Revision | DBO | Servers | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | on | 2 | 2/2 illegal memory access in round 1. With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` the trace points at `sparse_mla_attention.py:858` (`_forward_mqa_kernel` on the `stage_prefill_rows` cache) → `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` |
| main | off | 2 | 1/2 illegal memory access in round 2 |
| main + this PR | off | 2 | 768/768 requests 200 |
| main + this PR | on | 4 (+3 with launch blocking) | No illegal memory access. 2/4 servers die in round 1 from the separate #61487 crash (`dbo_register_recv_hook`, which hides microbatch 1's `CUDA error: invalid argument`); 0/3 with launch blocking |

The crash is not DBO-specific; DBO only makes it show up sooner. The remaining DBO failure is #61487 and is out of scope for this PR.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py                              # 15 passed
```

## Purpose

HiSparse's resident prefill conversion lazily gathers a batch-ordered copy of the residency table inside the layer-0 conversion. The gather is queued after `logical_topk_ready`, but the side-stream converter waits only on that event, so it can read the table before it's written.

This PR removes the gathered table. The sparse-MLA index remap kernel gets an optional `idx_mapping` indirection, off for other callers, and HiSparse passes its persistent residency table plus `request_state_indices` directly. Both are written before the forward, so the existing event orders them. Residency is stored group-major, so each group's view is a contiguous table.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Attention] Fix FlashInfer MLA DCP decode on ragged spec-decode batches
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59065

With DCP > 1 and speculative decoding, FlashInfer MLA decode crashes when the decode batch is ragged, i.e. requests carry different numbers of query tokens. That happens whenever a request has fewer drafts than the others, and also during warmup. For example, Kimi-K3 with `-tp 2 -dcp 2` and DSpark fails at engine startup:

```
ValueError: causal_seqlens_kv_global must have shape (9,), got (2,)
```

Here a 1+7 request and a 1-token request make 9 decode tokens.

DCP cannot take the compact ragged path (`cum_seq_lens_q`), because it needs LSE. So ragged batches fall to the "uneven length" branch. That branch has two problems:

- **Shape mismatch.** It splits `q` into one row per token, but it keeps `block_table`, `seq_lens` and `causal_seqlens_kv_global` per request. FlashInfer then rejects the call.
- **Silent wrong reshape.** The branch is only taken when `num_decode_tokens % num_decodes != 0`. A ragged batch whose token count happens to divide evenly (e.g. 8 + 2 tokens) is instead `view`ed as a uniform 5 + 5 batch, and each request's rows attend to the wrong KV.

## Fix

A batch is now treated as ragged when `num_decode_tokens != num_decodes * max_query_len`. Ragged causal batches are split into single-token rows:

- `block_table` and `seq_lens` are expanded per row with the existing `_flattened_decode_metadata`.
- Each row's DCP bound is `T - (tokens of its request after it)`. FlashInfer defines `causal_seqlens_kv_global` as the global exclusive causal bound of each row's newest query token, and `dcp_tot_seq_lens` (`T`) already includes all of the request's query tokens.

The non-DCP causal path is unchanged; it already goes through `cum_seq_lens_q`.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR touches this branch. #56784 edits the same file, but only for backend selection.

## Test Plan

- Kernel check on GB200, run directly against `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` with the cute-dsl backend, `cp_world=2`, both ranks, and `(T, q_len)` in `{(301, 8), (97, 8), (130, 4), (64, 1)}`:
  - One request with `q_len` rows and bound `T` gives bit-identical output and LSE (max error `0.0`) to `q_len` single-token rows bounded at `T - (q_len - 1 - j)`.
  - Negative control: bounding every split row at `T` gives a max output error of `0.26`.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py`: `test_flashinfer_mla_forward_uses_native_dcp_api` is extended with a ragged `(3, 1)` batch. The new `ragged-causal` case fails without this change and passes with it.

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py
```

## Test Result

- `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py` + `tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py`: 23 passed, 1 skipped (GB200).
- Without the source change, only `ragged-causal` fails.
- An end-to-end run with Kimi-K3 was not done here. The `dcp2-*-dspark` cases in #59229 are strict xfails for this bug and will flip once this lands.

No output changes for batches that worked before, so no model eval was run.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Reserve KDA prefill workspace before profiling
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Earlier Kimi K3 NVFP4 serving OOMs exposed approximately 0.93 GiB/rank of KDA prefill workspace growth after KV cache sizing. Although the latest tested stack now completes the workload without this patch, reserve that workspace before profiling so KV sizing accounts for the memory actually needed.

## Claims

- Reserve the configured FlashKDA layout or FlashInfer output layout before attention warmup.
- Reuse the shared, grow-only workspace across layers and subsequent requests within its capacity.
- Preserve construction without an initialized workspace manager and avoid reservations for the Triton prefill backend.

## Validation

The earlier OOM no longer reproduces in the latest matched GPU comparison on GB200 NVL with Kimi K3 NVFP4, TP16, default/profile-derived KV sizing, and `gpu_memory_utilization=0.95`:

| Measurement | Without reservation | With reservation |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| KV cache per rank | 21.42 GiB | 20.49 GiB |
| Lowest sampled GPU-0 free memory | 0.53 GiB | 1.69 GiB |
| Both configured serving sweeps, all request counts | Passed | Passed |

Both arms completed all configured requests in both sweeps without OOM or request errors. The reservation moves 0.93 GiB/rank into the budget before KV sizing and improves runtime headroom; throughput differed by at most approximately 1.6%. This supports correcting the accounting gap, without claiming the patch was required for these runs to pass.

This campaign used an exact-content port of commit `2e3f235a2197dfb95288a9b98266900ab9767ae4` to a pinned vLLM v0.30.0 stack. The FlashInfer workspace backport, MoE workspace caller port, and separate V2 graph-accounting fix were held constant in both arms. GPU results apply to this combination; the assessment of current upstream main is based on source inspection.

The focused regression suite at commit `796d49e802fb0adacb1b94466013b2d5f912d7cb` also passed on GB200 with this installed stack: **10 passed, zero skips or errors**. It uses real layer constructors and a two-layer dummy-weight model through `LLM`, including two-token generation with both FlashKDA and FlashInfer prefill. Removing only the reservation block in the disposable installed package caused all **six reservation/engine cases to fail**: four found no reserved storage and both engine cases rejected workspace growth before memory profiling. The original source was then restored.

<details>
<summary>GPU regression commands and observed results</summary>

With the reservation:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_workspace.py -v -rA -o addopts='' --junitxml=/tmp/kda-fixed.xml
10 passed in 92.91s
```

With only the constructor reservation block removed:

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_workspace.py -k 'reserved_and_shared or reservation_only_grows or engine_reserves' -v -rA -o addopts='' --junitxml=/tmp/kda-baseline.xml
6 failed, 4 deselected in 62.16s
AssertionError: Workspace is locked ... current size is 0.00 MB. Workspace growth is not allowed after locking.
```

JUnit checks confirmed the counts and zero skips or setup errors in both runs.

</details>

Confirmation on a second GB200 NVL cluster remains outstanding.

## Details

Upstream main inspected at [`eca54bd1`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/eca54bd1d937e778a939c240a2ed966fbcb12f85) still skips attention during V2 memory profiling and first requests KDA's prefill workspace during attention execution. That workspace can therefore grow during kernel warmup, after KV cache sizing. The passing control shows that the tested configuration has enough headroom despite this ordering; it does not mean the late allocation was included in the budget.

The worker initializes the workspace manager before model loading. Reserving immediately after the backend's layout is known brings the allocation into the model-loading memory measurement, reducing dependence on spare runtime headroom.

The reservation uses the same ordered specs and `get_simultaneous` call as runtime. Returned views are discarded; storage stays with the shared manager rather than each layer. FlashInfer's output scratch is reserved conservatively even when a particular request can write directly to the output. KV sizing settings and CUDA graph accounting are unchanged.

Duplicate-work check: searched open upstream PRs for `KDA workspace` and `workspace prefill in:title`; no matching KDA constructor-reservation fix was found. Related [#61250](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61250) changes prefill backend selection rather than adding this early reservation.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enable best-effort NUMA binding by default for eligible GPU multiprocessing launches, including PCP. Automatic mode prefers GPU-local memory; explicit binding retains its strict memory policy.

This continues [ivanium/vllm#53](https://github.com/ivanium/vllm/pull/53) by Yifan Qiao (@ivanium). His original commit `788505bea2c6cae925fce4afe47195188656896d` was cherry-picked with authorship, co-author trailers, and sign-offs preserved. The branch includes the merged shared GPU-indexing fix [#61237](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61237) and the CI bot's merge of main (`a1e1823967`, main parent `8977b13a1c`).

## Claims

- Validate fresh host-local GPU-to-NUMA topology in the launcher, then pass the decision and mapping to children. Preserve constrained CPU affinity and existing non-default memory policies in automatic mode.
- Automatically prefer GPU-local memory with `--preferred`; EngineCore uses `--preferred-many` for multi-node shards. Explicit `--numa-bind` or binding lists retain `--membind`. Failed automatic policy probes fall back to CPU-only, then unbound.
- Enable automatic binding for supported local PCP launches. GPU offsets include TP × PCP × PP for each DP shard, and EngineCore's CPU affinity covers its workers.
- Explicit NUMA CLI flags, including binding-list shortcuts, select `spawn` even when `fork` was requested. Omitted flags and `--no-numa-bind` leave start-method selection unchanged.

| Restricted CPU affinity, B200 | CPUs `0-7` preserved; automatic binding disabled; serving succeeded. |
| Inherited `--membind=0`, H200 | Existing `MPOL_BIND` preserved; automatic binding disabled. |
| Denied NUMA syscalls, H200 | Real seccomp `EPERM` for `get_mempolicy`, `set_mempolicy`, `mbind`; automatic binding disabled; serving succeeded. |
| 8 GiB container, 256 MiB CPU offload | Soft preference engaged; peak RAM 3.96 GiB versus 3.97 GiB with binding disabled; neither OOMed. |
| 8 GiB container, 16 GiB CPU offload | Both automatic and disabled modes were OOMKilled before readiness, without early capacity rejection. |

The five surviving canaries completed 512-token SSE, cached-prompt logprobs, tool calls/roundtrips, 400 load requests and 130 shape-valid constrained JSON responses. Each completed CPU-to-GPU restores (80–159 blocks), with unchanged pod UIDs and worker PIDs and zero new restarts. This validated exercised offload behavior, not production capacity. | `--numa-bind` | Strict `--membind`; missing numactl or undetectable topology remains an error. Existing policy-probe fallback applies. |
| `--no-numa-bind` | No vLLM-added binding. |
| `--numa-bind-nodes` / `--numa-bind-cpus` | Imply explicit enablement and strict memory policy. Combining with `--no-numa-bind` is rejected. |

An internal flag preserves automatic-policy identity after `numa_bind` resolves to `True`, so spawned workers do not mistake it for explicit strict binding. This launch-local state is excluded from the DP configuration hash; no public flag or steady-state inference operation is added.

Automatic eligibility requires CUDA/ROCm, multiple NUMA nodes, numactl and usable memory-policy support, known unrestricted CPU affinity, a default memory policy, and `spawn` with an `mp`/`uni` executor and `mp` DP, including supported PCP launches. Ray, external/custom launchers, device-ID remapping and fork remain excluded. Each launcher interprets NUMA IDs on its own host. The temporary PCP exclusion is removed now that the merged indexing prerequisite and actual bound PCP+DP launches have been verified.

Soft preference permits allocations on other allowed NUMA nodes when local memory is unavailable. Explicit strict binding still needs sufficient memory on the selected nodes. Existing loader RAM estimates and container limits are unchanged; policy probes check acceptance, not allocation capacity.

Unit coverage includes worker/EngineCore policies, fallback, config-copy/hash stability, PCT CPU selection, inherited policies, topology eligibility, CLI start-method selection and PCP/DP indexing. Existing NVIDIA/AMD `utils_` CI retains unit coverage. AMD/ROCm serving, native macOS runtime, hard `cpuset.mems` restrictions, mixed-socket PCP, multi-host PCP and actual preferred-memory spillover remain untested. No throughput or production offload-capacity claim is made. Remote CI build [#97587](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97587) exercised the PCP follow-up; its worker-import failure is addressed by `aeef060224`, with a retry requested.

Duplicate-work searches on 2026-10-15 found no competing upstream GPU automatic-default PR. This PR continues the credited fork trial; other NUMA work addressed affinity, memory sizing, CPU execution or ROCm packaging.

## Overview

Add a platform-selected backend so hardware plugins can reuse HiSparse's runtime and connector. CUDA uses the same cache operations and kernels.

Related: #60072. Ascend integration: vllm-project/vllm-ascend#19109.

## Claims

- Add `HiSparseBackend` for cache operations, host registration, IPC handles, resident-row payload handling, capture queries, DMA and statistics dtype.
- Let each platform select its HiSparse backend through a `@classmethod` hook. The base platform returns `None`; CUDA overrides the method in `platforms/cuda.py`.
- Validate cache formats before allocation and prepare device views inside the existing initialization rollback scope.
- Use `torch.Stream`, `torch.Event` and `torch.accelerator` directly for common device operations. Only IPC events need backend-specific creation/import/export. FP8 prefill keeps its existing custom-op call.

Speculative group prefetch is excluded. Follower staging keeps the original `decode_batch` condition. No CUDA performance improvement is claimed.

## Validation

- CPU fixture follow-up for [Buildkite #97663](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97663#01a17e0c-4bb9-473c-a68f-35f5ad9fe991): planning and configuration tests now select the real CUDA HiSparse backend through the platform hook instead of overriding the old CUDA predicates. Unsupported-platform checks use the hook's `None` result. On Linux/aarch64 with PyTorch 2.10 and an explicit CPU target, the command below gave `22 failed, 5 passed` at `5b8e00878206`, then `27 passed` with `bb13de1884ba`. ```

The default Qwen3-0.6B configuration was cached for both runs; no model weights were loaded.

- The platform selector and CUDA override use `@classmethod`, matching other platform backend hooks. Class/instance calls and descriptor inheritance were checked on the actual base class and exact CUDA method source. An independent audit of the exact Ascend override confirmed existing instance calls remain compatible; its matching classmethod override is still needed for class calls. This CPU descriptor check does not qualify device execution or the full Ascend pair.

- Whole-PR follow-up checked the eight changed vLLM modules and all 28 test files mentioning HiSparse, including 43 literal module patch targets. Existing connector tests now patch the accelerator/backend entry points, the row-DMA fixture initializes its backend, and resident-prefill gathering uses a bound runtime. Existing payload and ordering assertions are retained.
- The existing zero-token TP ordering regression reproduced four `AttributeError` failures on the removed patch target before the fix and passed all four parameters afterward. It used exact production/test definitions in an out-of-tree CPU runner. The draft-mirror runner reaches pinned allocation but cannot execute on CPU-only torch; device regressions remain unrun locally.

- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff check/format, mypy, typos, markdownlint-cli2, SPDX, import checks and test tethering. Python syntax and `git diff --check` passed.
- The two checked-in resident-gather cases passed with real CPU tensors and the actual `HiSparseBackend`, checking page stride, reordered/repeated rows and packed-byte payloads. An out-of-tree runner selected the unchanged test function to avoid full worker-module imports; no backend or torch methods were substituted. This is not a full vLLM pytest or device result.
- A real CUDA stream/IPC-event ordering regression was added to the existing attention suite; it is not run locally.
- Standard worker pytest collection was attempted on Windows with faulthandler and terminated with an access violation (exit `-1073741819`). CUDA/NPU model, graph replay, accuracy and performance validation remain pending.
- Hooks for untouched CUDA, workflow, shell, dependency and Rust files were skipped to avoid unrelated tool installation. No unfiltered full-hook run is claimed.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py -k hisparse
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -k hisparse

```

The existing Buildkite worker and attention suites select these files. Retained additions check real payload values and initialization rollback; mock-only backend routing tests have been removed.

A plugin overrides `Platform.get_hisparse_backend_cls()` with its backend's qualified class name. Lookup is lazy and cached by class name. commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Pass zero positions to the fused MLA decode q-prep kernel
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
Fixes a large accuracy regression for Kimi-K3 on ROCm when DCP is off (dcp1). It comes from the fused decode q-prep path added in #59634.

`KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper._fused_decode` gives AITER's `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla` a **one-row** identity cos/sin cache (K3 is NoPE). It also passes the **real** token positions, assuming the kernel clamps them into the cache.

That assumption is false on AITER v0.1.26. DeepSeek-shaped inputs now go to the head-grouped `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla_seg_kernel<PAGE_SIZE=0>`, which only clamps on the DCP (`compute_all_q_rope`) path:
- **One head per block**, i.e. every small decode batch (`T*H/num_CU <= 32`): cos/sin reads past the cache return 0. For every token at position ≥ 1, q_pe is written as **all zeros** and a wrong k_pe goes into the KV cache. This is silent.
- **More heads per block**: the kernel reads past the allocation and can fault (see ROCm/aiter#6879).

Since the RoPE here is the identity, position 0 gives exactly the right result for every token. This PR passes a preallocated all-zeros positions buffer, sliced to the kernel's token count (taken from `slot_mapping`). That removes the dependency on any AITER clamp behaviour.
- The buffer is allocated once in `__init__` as a non-persistent buffer, so captured CUDA graphs need no extra per-layer memset.
- The now-unused `positions` argument of `_fused_decode` is dropped.
- The comment that wrongly said the kernel clamps is corrected.

ROCm/aiter#6879 fixes the kernel side. This change keeps vLLM correct on AITER versions with or without that fix.

## Test Plan / Results
1. Kernel microtest (MI355X, AITER v0.1.26, T=8 and 64, H=12):

| cos/sin cache | positions | q_pe max err | q_pe fraction == 0 | cached k_pe max err |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 row | real (1 … 900000) | 2.9–3.8 | 1.00 | 2.0–3.1 |
| 1 row | **zeros (this PR)** | ≤ 0.125 (fp8 rounding) | 0 | ≤ 0.125 |
| full 1M rows | real | ≤ 0.125 | 0 | ≤ 0.11 |

2. End to end with the InferenceX agentic eval:
   - Setup: Kimi-K3 MXFP4, TP8, dcp1, DSpark k=7, max-num-seqs 8 (the CI conc=4 recipe).
   - Eval: Kimi-Vendor-Verifier `kimi_tool_call_schema_full`, 408 cases.
   - Image: `nightly-rocm100-df6603f0`.

| | score | DSpark mean AL |
|---|---|---|
| before | 0.740 | 2.95 |
| fused path disabled | 0.988 | 3.47 |
| **zero positions** (per-call `positions.new_zeros` patch, same kernel input as this PR) | **0.988** | **3.52** |
| old image, before #59634 | 0.983 | 3.25 |

   The same regression shows up in InferenceX run 39733293799: conc 1/2/4 (dcp1) score 0.75–0.78, while conc ≥ 10 (dcp8, fused path disabled) scores 0.97–0.995.

3. End to end with the c1 recipe from SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4393, using **this PR's `mla.py`** unchanged:
   - Setup: dcp1, max-num-seqs 1, DSpark k=7, `decode_backend=latency_specialized`, `kda_prefill_backend=fused`, Model Runner V2.
   - The specialized decode was active. Its MLA layers still go through `mla_attn.forward`, so they use the fused q-prep path.
   - Eval: same suite, run at concurrency 1 as in CI.

| | score |
|---|---|
| before ([InferenceX CI job](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39923143820/job/120542350622)) | 0.7819 |
| **this PR** | **0.9926 (405/408)** |

   The 3 remaining failures hit the 2048-token limit without emitting a tool call. That is the same small residual seen on the old image and in the runs above.

4. `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_mla_direct_return.py`: 5 passed.

## Notes
- Separate from this PR: K3 has 96 heads, so TP8 gives 12 heads per rank, padded to 16. `_fused_decode` allocates `q_out_padded` with `torch.empty`, so the padding heads 12–15 go to the asm MLA kernel uninitialized. Their outputs are discarded and heads are independent, so this looks benign, but it may be worth zero-filling.
