## Overview

Capture the DeepSeek-V4.1 decoder replay graphs on the model graphs' capture stream, so that they reuse the model graphs' free blocks in the shared graph pool instead of reserving a second pool. Fixes #62965.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill on GB200 (DP4, breakable PIECEWISE graphs up to 16384 tokens): graph capture memory drops from 15.52 GiB to 9.88 GiB per rank, and the replay capture no longer adds a graph pool segment.
- No accuracy or capture-time change beyond run-to-run noise (table below).
- Only the replay graphs move to the shared stream. The speculator and encoder captures, and Model Runner V1, keep a new stream per capture.

## Validation

GB200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1P1D, prefill DP4, `max_model_len` 16k, breakable PIECEWISE graphs with capture sizes up to 16384 tokens, DSpark on. Two fresh service starts per arm. Measured on a v0.32.0-based build with this change; see Details for what differs on `main`.

| | separate streams (`main`) | shared stream (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| prefill graph capture memory per rank | 15.52 / 15.52 GiB | 9.88 / 9.88 GiB |
| capture time | 36 / 36 s | 36 / 37 s |
| GSM8K (1319, greedy) | 97.50 / 97.42 | 97.57 / 97.12 |

- Before the change, `torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()` segments at the end of `capture_model()`, grouped by `(segment_pool_id, stream)`, show the replay graphs' own pool: 5.18 GiB reserved, none of it in use. After the change, the replay capture adds no graph pool segment.
- First-token top-20 logprobs on 64 prompts of 1k-7k tokens (prefix cache off, concurrency 1 and 16) differ across arms by as much as across two starts of the same arm. At concurrency 1: first token equal in 59-62/64 across arms vs. 60-61/64 within an arm; median |Δlogprob| of the first token 0.05-0.06 in both cases.

No test is added: CI has no runner for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with replay graphs, and the existing replay capture test (`tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py`) calls `capture_replay_graphs()` without a stream, so it keeps today's behavior.

## Details

**Root cause.** Since #59532, `DecoderReplayCudaGraphManager` captures the replay graphs after the model graphs, in a `CudaGraphManager.capture()` call of its own. Every `capture()` enters `graph_capture()`, which creates a new stream. Both managers capture into the global graph pool, but the caching allocator reuses a free block only on the stream that freed it, so the replay graphs cannot use the model graphs' free pool blocks and reserve their own.

**Change.**

- `graph_capture(device, stream=None)` reuses `stream` when one is given.
- `CudaGraphManager.capture(..., stream=None)` captures on it and records the stream it used in `capture_stream`.
- `GPUModelRunner.capture_model()` passes the model graphs' `capture_stream` to `ModelState.capture_inner_cudagraphs()`, and DeepSeek-V4.1 forwards it to `capture_replay_graphs()`.

**Why sharing is safe.** A replay graph runs inside an eager break of a model graph. `DecoderReplayCudaGraphManager.run()` first gathers the layer inputs into its static `input_buffers`, then replays. After the break, the model graph reads only the break's own output buffers (`DecoderReplayLayers._break_outputs`), which live outside the graph pool. KV caches and the replay batch metadata are persistent. So no model graph tensor in the pool is still needed while a replay graph runs.

The one exception is aux hidden states captured before the replay layers: the forward holds them across the break. `DecoderReplayLayers.has_early_aux()` reports whether any aux layer id is below the replay start, and in that case the replay graphs keep their own stream. For DSpark on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, the aux layers (37-39) are produced inside the replay layers (from layer 20 on), so the fallback does not apply there.

**Differences from the measured build.** The port to `main` also forwards the stream through the specialized decode model state's `capture_inner_cudagraphs()` override (#61868), and the `graph_capture()` change sits next to #57481's edits. The early-aux fallback is new in this PR. It returns `False` in the measured configuration, so the measured path is unchanged.

**Alternatives.**

- #59537 caches one capture stream per device for every `graph_capture()` call. It would also let the replay graphs reuse the model graphs' pool, but it puts the speculator capture on that stream as well. The speculator runs after the target forward and reads its outputs, so it needs its own lifetime argument. Passing the stream only to the graphs replayed inside the model graphs limits the change to the case argued above.
- Capturing the replay graphs nested inside the model graph capture, as #56752 did, also shares the pool, but then a replay graph is captured inside one model graph size and replayed inside others.
- Smaller `decoder_replay_cudagraph_capture_sizes` shrink the replay pool proportionally, but larger replay batches then run eagerly.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Avoid redundant tensor operations during serialization
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
Reduce GIL contention in EngineCore's output thread by avoiding redundant PyTorch operations when exporting contiguous CPU tensors for serialization. This is a follow-up of sorts to #61640, has a similar motivation, and addresses a similar problem, this time in the EngineCore output thread.


## Claims
- Improve embedding throughput on short inputs by **7.5% at concurrency 128** and **2.6% at concurrency 64** on the GH200 workload below, with no request errors.
- Reduce contiguous CPU FP32 export latency from **4.61 µs to 1.10 µs** and GIL releases from **7 to 1** per call.
- Reuse `TORCH_DTYPE_TO_NUMPY_DTYPE` to export NumPy-native dtypes directly and view other dtypes as uint8, avoiding exception overhead for BF16, FP8 and packed FP4.



## Validation

Existing serialization, buffer-lifetime, and prompt-embedding hashing tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/utils_/test_serial_utils.py \
  tests/v1/test_serial_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  -k 'serial or prompt_embeds' -q
```


**Review-fix validation:** 84 passed, 88 deselected with the command above. Coverage includes exact dtype, shape and byte round trips for 19 tensor dtypes as scalars and matrices. All pre-commit hooks passed.

A local CPU comparison against commit `22b25cb319` (2048 elements, minimum of 5 repeats of 5000 calls) reduced export time for `float8_e4m3fnuz`, `float8_e5m2fnuz`, `float8_e8m0fnu` and `float4_e2m1fn_x2` from 14.6–14.9 µs to 2.24–2.26 µs. FP32/BF16 timings were effectively unchanged. Exception tracing confirmed these FP8/FP4 formats export without entering the exception path. The GH200 serving measurements below predate this review fix and have not been rerun.

**End-to-end performance**: `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16` (`--quantization fp8_per_tensor`,
  `--api-server-count 16`), `/v1/embeddings`, ViDoRe v3 finance-en queries (~30 tokens each),
  closed-loop client on the other NUMA node, 1× GH200, `orjson` in use. Mean of 3 × 30 s runs.

  | Concurrency | Metric | main | this PR | Change |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 64 | Throughput (req/s) | 4,482 | 4,600 | **+2.6%** |
  | 64 | p50 latency (ms) | 14.26 | 13.87 | −2.7% |
  | 64 | p99 latency (ms) | 14.97 | 15.04 | +0.5% |
  | 128 | Throughput (req/s) | 6,601 | 7,093 | **+7.5%** |
  | 128 | p50 latency (ms) | 19.37 | 18.04 | −6.9% |
  | 128 | p99 latency (ms) | 20.72 | 18.85 | −9.0% |

  **Per call** (`tensor_data()` on a contiguous 2048-element CPU tensor):

  | dtype | main | this PR | Speedup | GIL releases (main → PR) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | float32 | 4.61 µs | 1.10 µs | 4.2× | 7 → 1 |
  | float16 | 4.44 µs | 1.10 µs | 4.1× | — |
  | bfloat16 | 4.78 µs | 3.83 µs | 1.25× | 7 → 3 |
  | float8_e4m3fn | 4.53 µs | 3.84 µs | 1.18× | — |
## Details
The original chain releases and reacquires the GIL repeatedly even when the tensor is already contiguous and on CPU. This overhead adds contention when the output thread serializes many small tensors during concurrent serving.

The fast path exports a NumPy-backed byte memoryview directly. Membership in the existing `TORCH_DTYPE_TO_NUMPY_DTYPE` mapping identifies NumPy-native dtypes; other dtypes are viewed as uint8 before export. The mapping includes native real floating-point, integer and boolean dtypes. This preserves raw bytes without another dtype registry or unnecessary `.view()` calls for the listed native types. Noncontiguous or non-CPU tensors, and failed exports (including BF16 scalars), use the original conversion chain.

[by Claude Code]

## Overview

Follow-up to #62543, #63394 and #63534. This PR first added two rows to the guide's GB200 AgentX table: TP8 at concurrency 5 and TP4 at concurrency 22. It now expresses the MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 GB200 AgentX lane (Dynamo + vLLM, aggregated) from [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4281](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4281) as two opt-in presets with its eight measured points. #63534 did the same for the H200, B200 and B300 lanes. Picking a point renders the worker's flags, environment and pinned image.

## Claims

- A preset point can't change the strategy, so the two-tray TP8 points need their own preset:
  - `gb200_agentx` ("AgentX TP4", `single_node_tp`, one 4-GPU tray):
    - GPU-resident KV: `tp4_c1`, `tp4_c10`;
    - SimpleCPUOffload host KV: `tp4_c20`, `tp4_c22`, `tp4_c25`, `tp4_c30`.
  - `gb200_agentx_tp8` ("AgentX TP8", `multi_node_tp`, two trays): `tp8_c1`, `tp8_c5`.
- Both presets share:
  - the source: key `minimaxm3-fp4-gb200-dynamo-vllm-agentic-agg-mtp`, `source.revision` `bbebca8b4be98a06401e943bad37874abbd65101`;
  - the image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-5555a2d8…@sha256:8896fd7b…` and Dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261016`;
  - the GQA EAGLE3 draft, text-only mode and **Thinking Always On**. Thinking Always On matches the other AgentX presets and the lane's client, which asked for thinking on every request.
- Each point sets its own `--max-num-seqs` and CUDA graph capture sizes. The offload points also set the lane's host KV budget: 181 GiB per rank, lazy offload.
- The guide's GB200 section now links to the presets in place of its table and worker command. The TP4 runbook keeps the etcd, NATS, Dynamo worker and frontend steps. It also says what changes under `python3 -m dynamo.vllm`:
  - drop the API-server flags the builder adds;
  - keep thinking on per request or with `--dyn-default-thinking-mode enabled`.
- A GB200 note keeps the old guide's warning: the KV Offload → Simple default (220 GiB per rank) overcommits a tray's host memory.
- Outside `presets`, `notes`, `guide` and two YAML comments, the parsed recipe equals `main`, so commands built without a preset don't change.

## Validation

- The InferenceX PR's sweep at `bbebca8b` passed all eight points. Each point's eval jobs, which keep real block verification, passed too:
  - GSM8K 0.953 at TP4 C22;
  - the MiniMax-M3 eval set 0.99 at TP4 C22 and TP8 C5.
- A local check script (not part of this PR) layers base, variant, strategy, preset, point, features and KV offload the way `command-synthesis.js` and `recipe-presets.js` do.
  - For each of the eight points, it compares the result with the InferenceX recipe: base plus that point's override.
  - All eight match, apart from the exclusions below and the `vllm serve` equivalents of the lane's Dynamo frontend and client: `--tool-call-parser`, `--enable-auto-tool-choice` and `--default-chat-template-kwargs`.
  - For TP4 C22, TP8 C1 and TP8 C5, it also matches the worker commands in the sweep logs, minus the synthetic-acceptance keys.
  - The script emulates the renderer; it isn't the renderer.
- I didn't run the renderer's strict `validate-source.mjs` build or `pre-commit` locally, because both need a dependency install.
  - The PR's `Recipes / Validate` check runs that strict build: it renders every preset at every point and fails on any error. It passed on the previous commit.
  - `pre-commit` also runs in CI.
  - After this push, I'll check both preset JSONs and the Presets tab on the Vercel preview against the same expectations. I'll tick Testing and Validation once the check and the preview pass.
- `git diff --check` is clean. The branch merges cleanly with `main` and with #63810.

## Details

- Not a duplicate. The only other open PR on this file is #63810, which changes the B300 preset. `meta.date_updated` is left as is so the two PRs don't conflict.
- Left out, judged by effect:
  - synthetic acceptance (`rejection_sample_method`, `synthetic_acceptance_length`): a benchmark control that fixes the acceptance rate; production serving keeps block verification;
  - AIPerf settings: these configure the benchmark client, not the server;
  - Slurm, health-check, etcd-lease, container and placement settings, `--device-ids` and `--dump-config-to`: cluster and harness plumbing;
  - `--kv-cache-metrics`, `VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL` and OTEL: telemetry only;
  - `UCX_TLS` and `UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE`: only a NIXL KV transfer would use them, and these workers have none;
  - `UCX_NET_DEVICES` and `NCCL_IB_HCA`: the site's own device names;
  - `--served-model-name` (it equals the model id) and `--pipeline-parallel-size 1` (the default).
- The schema's `image.dynamo` holds a commit, and the Presets tab shortens it to 8 characters. The lane installed Dynamo from PyPI, so the version pins are in `image.pip`.
- Please don't merge yet. A TP4 SimpleCPU point at concurrency 15 is in the InferenceX PR's next sweep. Once that sweep passes, I'll add `tp4_c15` here and bump `source.revision` to match.

Thanks for taking a look!

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Detect Lark grammars like the Python engine
commits.pr_body:
## Overview The Rust frontend's `answer_format` decides whether a request's `structured_outputs.grammar` is XGrammar EBNF, and so can be composed into a parser-built output grammar, or another syntax such as Lark, which stays on its own wire field. It treated any grammar containing `::=` as EBNF. This ports Python's `grammar_is_likely_lark`, which the engine's xgrammar backend also uses for a grammar left on its wire field, so both frontends and the engine agree on a grammar's syntax. ## Claims - A Lark grammar whose comment mentions `::=` (e.g. `// Like root ::= "a" in EBNF.`) is no longer composed as an EBNF `grammar` leaf, which XGrammar fails to compile. It stays on its wire field, where the engine compiles it as Lark, as it would for the same request on the Python frontend's native path. - An EBNF grammar with `#` or `//` comments is still composed. ## Validation - `cargo nextest run -p vllm-chat --lib`: 427 passed; `cargo clippy -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean. - Red-green: with the old `contains("::=")` rule restored, `answer_format_leaves_other_constraints_on_their_wire_field` fails on the new Lark-with-comment case (`left: Some(Grammar(..))`, `right: None`). - Differential against Python's `grammar_is_likely_lark` source on 15 inputs (empty, comments with `#`/`//`, `#` or `//` inside string literals, tabs, `\r\n`, `::=` inside a Lark string literal): no mismatch. - XGrammar 0.2.8, for the misclassified input: as an EBNF `grammar` leaf inside a structural tag it fails (`EBNF lexer error at line 1, column 1: Unexpected character: /`); through `Grammar.from_lark`, the engine's path for a native Lark grammar, it compiles. - No model run: the change only selects between two existing paths, both covered by the tests above. ## Details - The rule is Python's, line by line: a grammar is Lark unless some line, before its first `#` or `//`, contains `::=`; an empty grammar counts as EBNF. Python's comment stripping also cuts at `#` or `//` inside string literals; it is kept as is, because the point is to match the engine's own classification of the same string, not to improve on it on one side. - Out of scope: a Lark grammar still cannot be composed on Rust, because XGrammar's structural-tag `grammar` leaf accepts only EBNF and Rust has no counterpart of Python's `Grammar.from_lark` conversion. That limitation predates this PR (vllm-project/vllm#60781) and is unchanged here. - Not a duplicate: no open PR touches Rust Lark detection. ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Bump fastokens to 0.3.5
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The Rust frontend pins fastokens 0.2.1, whose regex split cache can give a prompt different token ids from Hugging Face depending on the previous prompt encoded on the same thread. This PR bumps fastokens to 0.3.5, which fixes the cache, and keeps the current non-truncating behavior. It covers the Rust frontend part of #63467.

## Claims

- Fixes wrong token ids for prompts that share a ≥4 KiB prefix with the previous prompt on the same thread and diverge inside a whitespace run, e.g. deeper indentation or a newline after trailing spaces. No error is raised today: the wrong ids decode to the same text.
- Ignores `tokenizer.json`'s `truncation` and `padding` in both backends, as the Python frontend does: transformers resets both on every call, and a few published checkpoints set `truncation.max_length` to 512–4096. fastokens 0.3.4+ starts applying them on encode, so the fastokens path clears them to keep main's behavior. The `tokenizers` fallback already applied them on main, silently cutting prompts for such a checkpoint when fastokens couldn't load it; it now clears them too.
- Tokenizers that 0.2.1 rejects (e.g. a `Replace` normalizer or `ByteFallback`/`Strip` decoders, as in Gemma 4) now load with fastokens instead of the `tokenizers` fallback.

## Validation

Served reproducer with `vllm-rs serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` and `vllm-mock-engine` (aarch64). For each pair, one client sends B once, then A and B alternately 20 times to `/tokenize`, and compares each result with Hugging Face `tokenizers`:

| Pair | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ~6 KB prose + `def f():` with 4- vs 8-space indent | B wrong 20/21 | 0/21 |
| 5000 spaces + `x` vs 5000 spaces + `\n` | B wrong 20/21 | 0/21 |

A calls were right on both builds. The same pairs at crate level are wrong on 0.2.1 and right on 0.3.4 for the Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Llama 3.2, gpt-oss and GLM tokenizers. DeepSeek-V3.2 is right on both.

- New test `fastokens_encode_does_not_depend_on_previous_input` fails on main and passes here. The fixture uses a split regex with Qwen's whitespace alternatives and a `Ġ Ġ` merge, so the pieces' boundaries show up in the ids.
- `assert_ordinary_matches_added_empty` now asserts for both backends that the fixture's `truncation` is ignored. The fastokens test fails without `set_truncation(None)`, and the HF test fails without `with_truncation(None)`.
- `cargo test --workspace` (2307 passed) and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.
- Gemma 4, TinyLlama, ERNIE-4.5 and LFM2.5 tokenizers, which move off the `tokenizers` fallback: 0 encode and 0 decode differences from Hugging Face on 400 text slices each (37 B–40 KB).
- Encode cost with the Qwen3 tokenizer, 320 prompts of 128 KB each, 32 cores. CPU time per prompt drops from 8.1 / 7.0 / 6.0 ms to 1.25 / 1.13 / 1.10 ms at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32. Wall time per batch drops from 296 / 115 / 89 ms to 54 / 53 / 52 ms.

## Details

Root cause: fastokens' regex `Split` keeps a thread-local cache of the previous input's matches. When the next input shares at least 4096 bytes with it, matches ending inside the shared prefix are reused. Whitespace alternatives such as `\s+(?!\S)` and `\s*[\r\n]+` depend on bytes past the end of the match: in `"    x"` the run stops one space early, and with `\n` there the whole run is one piece. So a reused match near the divergence point can be wrong. crusoecloud/fastokens#78 (released in 0.3.4) reuses only matches that end before the whitespace run leading up to the unseen bytes. 0.3.5 adds a Python-binding deadlock fix and opt-in caches, and does not change the default encode path.

Changes in `hf.rs`:

- fastokens 0.3 adds `Decoder` variants. `is_byte_level_only` treats `Fuse` as a no-op, as before (0.2.1 parsed it as an empty `Sequence`). The new transforming decoders disqualify the byte-level decode fast path.
- `new_fastokens` and `new_hf` clear truncation and padding after loading.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Bound prefix cache reuse by the first requested prompt score
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `prompt_logprob_token_ids` and `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False`, a cache hit can skip requested scores. Cap prefix reuse at `prompt_logprob_start` so those rows are recomputed.

## Claims

Reuse the unscored prefix without dropping requested scores. Cache reads remain disabled by default for prompt scoring.

## Validation

Ten targeted cases, the Qwen3-0.6B model test and pre-commit passed. Batch-invariant scores matched exactly, including a single-host NIXL check. Default BF16 returned complete scores but differed by up to 0.29844; the cause remains unresolved.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction: environment, complete script and before/after results</summary>

On main `ab905a885d`, real Qwen3-0.6B/MMLU scoring reproduced:

```text
AssertionError: Missing scores: skip_cache=False, cached=32, first_scored_row=27
```

With candidate `6344014bb8`, 32 requests containing 184 scored rows matched exactly across eight cache-on/cache-off runs in batch-invariant mode. They also matched main with cache reads disabled. Qwen3-0.6B revision: `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`; dataset: `cais/mmlu`, revision `c30699e8356da336a370243923dbaf21066bb9fe`, first eight high_school_biology/test questions and all four options. Hardware: RTX 5090; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. This checks score completeness and consistency, not MMLU accuracy.

A separate default compiled/CUDA graph run passed start offsets 0, 31, 32 and 33, with 0, 16, 32 and 32 cached tokens respectively. The cached scores matched uncached scores at the existing numerical tolerances.

A later H200 check with Qwen3-0.6B and three candidate IDs returned the complete
123-row matrix and reused 16 tokens. Default BF16 execution differed from the
uncached scores by up to 0.29844, failing `atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-3`. The same test
with batch-invariant execution matched exactly. This does not establish default
execution score equivalence or fully attribute the numerical difference.

Historical regression validation of `6344014bb8` first recorded 317 passed and
69 failed. After unsetting the allocator environment configuration, rerunning
the 69 failed cases passed. This covers 386 cases across two runs, not a single

```python
import argparse
import atexit
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams, TokensPrompt


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
    model = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"
    revision = "c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca"
    data = pq.read_table(Path(__file__).with_name("mmlu.parquet")).slice(0, 8).to_pylist()
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model, revision=revision)
    prompts, starts = [], []
    for row in data:
        context = tokenizer.encode("Question: " + row["question"] + "\nAnswer:", add_special_tokens=False)
        for option in row["choices"]:
            suffix = tokenizer.encode(" " + option, add_special_tokens=False)
            ids = (context + suffix)[-4095:]
            prompts.append(TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=ids))
            starts.append(len(ids) - len(suffix) - 1)
    assert len(prompts) == 32 and min(starts) >= 0
    llm = LLM(
        model=model, revision=revision, dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=4096,
        max_num_seqs=128, max_num_batched_tokens=8192,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.65, enforce_eager=True, seed=233,
    )
    atexit.register(llm.llm_engine.engine_core.shutdown, timeout=30)
    arms = []
    # The first pair warms scorer kernels; retain three further pairs for timing.
    for skip in [True, False] * 4:
        assert llm.reset_prefix_cache()
        llm.generate(prompts, SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1), use_tqdm=False)
        params = [
            SamplingParams(
                temperature=0, max_tokens=1, prompt_logprob_start=start,
                prompt_logprob_token_ids=[[token] for token in p["prompt_token_ids"][start + 1:]],
                skip_reading_prefix_cache=skip,
            )
            for p, start in zip(prompts, starts)
        ]
        begin = time.perf_counter()
        outputs = llm.generate(prompts, params, use_tqdm=False)
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - begin
        rows = []
        for output, p, start in zip(outputs, prompts, starts):
            scores = output.prompt_token_id_logprobs
            assert scores is not None, (
                f"Missing scores: skip_cache={skip}, cached={output.num_cached_tokens}, "
                f"first_scored_row={start}"
            )
            assert scores.shape == (len(p["prompt_token_ids"]) - start - 1, 1)
            assert 0 <= (output.num_cached_tokens or 0) <= start
            rows.append({"scores": scores.tolist(), "cached_tokens": output.num_cached_tokens})
        arms.append({"skip_cache": skip, "elapsed_s": elapsed, "rows": rows})
        args.output.write_text(json.dumps({"prompts": prompts, "starts": starts, "arms": arms}))
        print("ARM", len(arms), skip, elapsed, sum(r["cached_tokens"] or 0 for r in rows), flush=True)
    for arm in arms[1:]:
        for reference, actual in zip(arms[0]["rows"], arm["rows"]):
            np.testing.assert_allclose(actual["scores"], reference["scores"], atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-3)
    assert any(r["cached_tokens"] for r in arms[1]["rows"])
    print("INTERVAL_OK", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

## Details

Both cache lookup paths use the same limit. Ordinary `prompt_logprobs` disable reuse. Connector requests set the skip flag before admission to prevent prompt truncation; MoRIIO's existing hybrid-producer hook ignores this flag and remains unverified.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Enable DeepGEMM sparse MQA logits on the FP8 indexer cache, DSv4.1
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`attention_config.indexer_sparse_logits` (#56254) lets DeepSeek-V4.1's candidate-consuming indexer layers score only the candidate blocks with DeepGEMM's sparse MQA-logits kernels instead of dense logits over the whole context. Today it requires the MXFP4 indexer cache (`indexer_kv_dtype="mxfp4"`), so with the default FP8 cache the flag fails at startup:

```
ValueError: attention_config.indexer_sparse_logits requires the MXFP4 indexer cache
```

The restriction dates from before #61149: the FP8 cache then stored one fp32 scale per token, while the sparse kernels take UE8M0-packed (granularity-32) scales. Since #61149, the SM100 FP8 indexer cache stores each token's power-of-two scale as four equal UE8M0 bytes, which is exactly the MXFP8 layout DeepGEMM expects, and DeepGEMM's sparse kernels already have an FP8 (`float_e4m3_t`, `SM100_MMA_MXF8F6F4_SS`) variant for both the contiguous (prefill) and paged (decode) paths. Its paged accessor reads the same page layout as vLLM's FP8 cache (`PAGE_KV x 128` value bytes, then `PAGE_KV` uint32 scales).

This PR wires the FP8 cache into the existing sparse path, so the decode speedup no longer requires trading the K cache down to 4 bits.

## Results

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, 4x B300, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, greedy decoding. Decode and prefill throughput from a linear fit of wall time against output length (256 / 1024 / 2048 output tokens), each point run twice

| batch x context | decode tok/s MAIN | decode tok/s PR | decode speedup | prefill tok/s MAIN | prefill tok/s PR | prefill speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 x 8K | 6,459 | 6,584 | 1.02x | 124,569 | 126,088 | 1.01x |
| 32 x 100K | 3,920 | 4,117 | 1.05x | 117,066 | 117,774 | 1.01x |
| 16 x 256K | 2,293 | 2,535 | 1.11x | 103,739 | 104,733 | 1.01x |
| 8 x 512K | 1,301 | 1,399 | 1.08x | 85,609 | 87,355 | 1.02x |
| 4 x 1M | 692 | 745 | 1.08x | 62,604 | 63,967 | 1.02x |

Decode improves at every point, with up to 11% higher decode throughput. Prefill is at parity: decoder SWA bounded replay (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58132) runs the candidate-consuming layers on only each request's last 128 tokens during prefill, so little prefill indexer work is left for the sparse path to remove.

## Overview

`_build_transfer_params` groups the same block ids again for every registered region and builds each descriptor in a Python loop. This PR groups once per KV group and request and computes each region's descriptors with NumPy. The output is unchanged: same values, same order, Python ints.

The branch is rebased on #63142 and keeps its normalization. That PR reduces how many descriptors there are; this one makes building the remaining ones cheap. Related: RFC #63006.

## Claims

Measured against main `41f5146b5`, which includes #63142.

- In a 1P1D serving run, `_build_transfer_params` takes 0.77 ms instead of 12.8 ms on fragmented calls (median). Those calls are about half of all calls under load.
- Mean TTFT drops by 6.5 / 10.8 / 7.9 ms at 3 / 5 / 6 req/s. The paired 95% CIs exclude zero.
- Greedy outputs are identical to main.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (nightly `41f5146b5`, `huggingface-hub==1.31.0` as in CI): `test_mooncake_connector.py` and `test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py` give 140 passed on main and 146 passed with this PR. The 6 new tests cover run boundaries, and fragmented ids that #63142 does not merge. The hybrid test now patches `_contiguous_runs`.

**Equivalence.** I extracted `_build_transfer_params` from main and from this PR and ran both on 2,000 randomized inputs. Inputs covered multiple layers, KV groups, Mamba null blocks, shared packed regions, heterogeneous TP, non-coalescible rows and prefix trimming. Outputs were identical.

**Microbenchmark.** One request through the real method, 64 KiB regions, Xeon 8358P:

| Layers × blocks | Block ids | Descriptors | main | this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 28 × 224 | ascending or jointly descending | 28 | 1.93 ms | 0.38 ms |
| 28 × 224 | random | 6,272 | 13.07 ms | 0.80 ms |
| 64 × 500 | random | 32,000 | 74.50 ms | 2.54 ms |

**End to end.**
- Setup: 1P1D on two hosts, A800 + ConnectX-6 200 Gb/s, DeepSeek-MoE-16B BF16, TP=1, block size 16, no prefix caching, `mooncake_connector_proxy.py`.
- Load: open-loop Poisson arrivals of 3,584-token prompts, 80 per rate, with the same seed for every run.
- Runs alternated main / PR / PR / main, and requests were compared pairwise.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `_build_transfer_params`, fragmented calls, median / p90 | 12.83 / 20.08 ms | 0.77 / 1.32 ms |
| `_build_transfer_params`, other calls, median | 2.73 ms | 0.45 ms |
| TTFT Δ, 3 / 5 / 6 req/s (paired mean, 95% CI) | — | −6.5 [−9.9, −3.1] / −10.8 [−15.4, −6.4] / −7.9 [−13.2, −2.5] ms |
| TTFT p50 Δ, single 3,584-token request | — | −11.5 ms |

Block ids under this load stay fragmented after #63142. Only about 1% of requests merge into one run. The median request (224 blocks) has 101 runs per layer, down from 213 without #63142.

## Details

- After #63142's normalization, block ids are the same for every region of a KV group. So `_contiguous_runs` computes the runs once per `(group_index, shared_group_ids)`, and each region's addresses come from one NumPy expression. Regions are visited in the original order. Heterogeneous TP, replicated KV, shared packed regions and Mamba handling are unchanged. `_contiguous_runs` replaces `group_concurrent_contiguous`.
- #60605 rewrites that same helper. Before #63142, on the same setup, a fragmented call took 2.7 ms with #60605 and 0.7 ms with this PR. If this one is preferred, I'm happy to carry over its tests and credit @feidudeqiu.

- **`seq_starts` on the NVFP4 gather kernel** instead of a block-table shim. `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache` gains an optional `seq_starts` like its fp8 twin (`token_offset = out_token - workspace_starts[req] + seq_starts[req]`), and the dense dispatch passes `chunk.starts` exactly as the `fp8_ds_mla` branch does. `shift_block_table_to_starts`, its alignment precondition, the clamp, the per-chunk gather and its CPU test are gone. Other callers are unchanged (the argument defaults to `None`).
- **Dropped the `MLACommonMetadataBuilder` workspace hunk and the `fp8_query` test arm.** `nvfp4_ds_mla` is only accepted by `FlashMLASparseBackend`, whose builder (`SparseMLACommonMetadataBuilder`) allocates its own BF16 workspace and hard-codes a BF16 prefill query, so neither was reachable.
- **DCP is rejected at startup** (`VllmConfig.validate_nvfp4_kv_cache_with_mla`) instead of in the per-layer forward on the first request with context; covered by `tests/test_config.py::test_nvfp4_ds_mla_rejects_decode_context_parallelism`.
- The raw `kv_c_and_k_pe_cache` pass is intentional: the `nvfp4_ds_mla` cache is allocated as `torch.uint8`. The three other gather dispatch sites that still send `nvfp4_ds_mla` to the generic gather (`mla_attention.py` DCP path, `kimi_k3/nvidia/mla.py`, `sparse_mla_attention.py`) are unreachable today and left for a follow-up.

Verification on the rebased head (`dc6aa4ae53`, B300 SM103, from-source build): **17 passed, 0 failed** — `test_mla_prefill_context_nvfp4.py` (1, the `seq_starts` path on real NVFP4 rows), `test_mla_context_chunks.py` (14), `test_config.py::test_nvfp4_ds_mla_rejects_decode_context_parallelism` (2); registered schema `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache(..., int batch_size, Tensor? seq_starts=None)`; torch 2.14.0+cu130, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.3a`. `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k nvfp4`: 27 passed including `test_cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache_with_seq_starts`.

## Purpose

`--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla` crashes in the MLA chunked-context prefill:

```
mla_attention.py  _compute_prefill_context
_custom_ops.py    gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache
RuntimeError: get_fp8_kv_cache_data_type, csrc/attention/dtype_fp8.cuh:34,
              Unsupported fp8 kv cache data type: nvfp4_ds_mla
```

`MLACommonBaseImpl._compute_prefill_context` gathers each chunk's cached context KV into a BF16 workspace. It has a branch for `fp8_ds_mla`; every other dtype goes to `gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache`, which only knows the fp8 variants. The NVFP4 upconvert kernel added with the `nvfp4_ds_mla` format, `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache`, is never called here.

Sparse MLA reaches this path through its dense-MHA prefill: a prefill whose total length is `<= index_topk` and that has cached context. In practice:

- **speculative-decoding warm-up**: the dummy batch takes this path, so an engine with `nvfp4_ds_mla` KV and a DFlash draft never finishes starting;
- **chunked prefill splitting a short prompt**: the continuation step has context;
- **prefix-cache hits** on short prompts.

Longer prefills use the sparse FlashMLA kernels, which already handle `nvfp4_ds_mla`.

**Fix:**

- Route `nvfp4_ds_mla` to `cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache`.
- Give that kernel an optional `seq_starts` (csrc + bindings + `_custom_ops`), mirroring `cp_gather_and_upconvert_fp8_kv_cache`: a continuation chunk reads from its context start instead of the request's first token. Without it, every chunk after the first would silently re-read the request's first tokens.
- Reject `nvfp4_ds_mla` with decode context parallelism at config validation; that combination is not validated.

Other dtypes are unaffected. I found no existing issue or PR for this.

## Test Plan

New tests:

- `tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_context_nvfp4.py` (SM100). Writes random KV into an `nvfp4_ds_mla` cache with `concat_and_cache_mla`, then runs `_compute_prefill_context` on it. The reference is the same method on a BF16 cache holding the dequantized values, through the generic gather. Every chunk must see bit-identical Q/K/V; the batch includes a chunk that continues one request and starts another.
- `tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py::test_cp_gather_and_upconvert_nvfp4_kv_cache_with_seq_starts` (SM100): the kernel's `seq_starts` with non-block-aligned starts, bit-exact against a full gather.
- `tests/test_config.py::test_nvfp4_ds_mla_rejects_decode_context_parallelism` (CPU).

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_mla_prefill_context_nvfp4.py tests/v1/attention/test_mla_context_chunks.py tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py tests/test_config.py -k "nvfp4 or context_chunks"
```

End-to-end on 1 × GB200 node (4 GPUs), run with the first revision of this change (block-table shift; same gather semantics):

- **Model:** GLM-5.3 (NVFP4 weights) + DFlash2 draft (fp8 KV, k=4).
- **Engine:** aggregated TP4, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4_ds_mla`, `--block-size 1024`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, prefix caching on.
- **Arms:** the same build with and without this change, plus an fp8-KV reference at `--max-model-len 262144`, since fp8 cannot fit one 1M-token request on TP4.
- **Checks:** startup; 6 distinct verifiable prompts, sequential then 12-way concurrent × 3 rounds; 12 concurrent ~1.7K-token prompts with `--max-num-seqs 8` and an 8192-token budget so some are necessarily split and their continuation runs this path, compared with the same prompts served unsplit; draft acceptance over 3 × 400 tokens on a short and a ~10K-token prompt.

## Test Result

**Unit tests:** see Status above for the current head. The first revision, on GB200 against `v0.30.1rc0`: the SM100 test failed before the change (`Unsupported fp8 kv cache data type: nvfp4_ds_mla`) and passed with it.

**End-to-end (first revision):**

| | without the change | **with the change** | fp8 KV reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| startup | crashes in warm-up (trace above) | serves | serves (at 256K) |
| KV capacity at 1M, TP4 | — | 1,646,592 tokens (1.57×) | does not fit one 1M request |
| correctness, 42 requests | — | 42 / 42 | 42 / 42 |
| forced split prefill, 36 requests | — | 36 / 36, identical to unsplit | 36 / 36, identical to unsplit |
| draft acceptance, short prompt | — | 39.0% | 37.7% |
| draft acceptance, ~10K-token prompt | — | 48.1% | 47.4% |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse][KV Connector] Fix DecodeBenchConnector crash on bounded KV cache groups
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`HiSparse` + `DecodeBenchConnector` **crashes** on `GLM-5.3` when `ISL > device_buffer_size(4096)`.

```
AssertionError: DecodeBenchConnector block range exceeds allocated blocks: request=chatcmpl-bd27629bd71bb94d-9ff77f54, group=22, range=[0, 87), allocated=64
```

The assertion fires in the scheduler on the first qualifying request, EngineCore goes fatal, and the whole serve instance dies. ISL ≤ 4096 passes only coincidentally (see Root Cause).

## Reproduction

Single 8xH200 node, TP8, vllm 0.32.0:

```
vllm serve /models/GLM-5.3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --max-model-len 256000 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[{"kv_connector":"DecodeBenchConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{}},{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}}]}}'
```

The assert above comes from this exact setup, on the first request with ~5.5k tokens.

## Root Cause

HiSparse (in-tree since v0.32.0, #60072) adds per-request hot-cache groups via `HiSparseHotSpec` — a direct `KVCacheSpec` subclass with a bounded allocation of `blocks_per_request = cdiv(device_buffer_size, block_size)` blocks. These groups opt out of external KV transfer (`enable_kv_transfer=False`, `vllm/v1/hisparse/layout.py`): they are ephemeral per-request replicas rebuilt from their transferable source group after a connector load. `DecodeBenchConnector.update_state_after_alloc` assumes every non-`CircularBufferSpec` group is token-paged and asserts the computed token range fits the allocation.

The numbers in the assert, decoded:

- `allocated=64`: the hot group's per-request cap — `cdiv(device_buffer_size=4096, block_size=64) = 64`, unrelated to sequence length.
- `range=[0, 87)`: the token-paged formula `cdiv(total_computed_tokens, 64)` for the request's ~5.5k tokens.
- Hence the crash is deterministic for any request with ISL > 4096, and ISL ≤ 4096 passes only because `cdiv(ISL, 64) ≤ 64` by coincidence.
- `group=22` is one of the 78 `hisparse_hot` groups of GLM-5.3.

## Fix

Skip groups that opted out of external KV transfer (i.e. groups missing from `KVCacheConfig.transfer_group_ids`): select no blocks for them at fill-scheduling time, the same way startup-fill groups are already handled. NIXL/Mooncake already key off `transfer_group_ids`; no new spec-shape heuristic is introduced.

This also aligns the fill side with the connector's load-side declaration: `get_loaded_kv_cache_group_ids()` defaults to `prefix_cacheable_group_ids`, which already excludes these groups. Skipping them additionally avoids selecting the 78 `hisparse_hot` layers that are absent from the connector's `kv_caches` (previously warned about on every request).

Groups with `enable_kv_transfer=True` (circular buffers, Mamba, sliding-window attention included) take exactly the same paths as on main — token-range math and the in-range assert are unchanged — so no currently working configuration changes behavior.

## Validation

- New regression test `test_decode_bench_connector_skips_non_transfer_groups`: builds a group from the real in-tree `HiSparseHotSpec` with `enable_kv_transfer=False` and asserts its entry in `reqs_to_fill` is empty; no checkpoint needed, runs in the existing kv_connector CI job. **Fails on main's `decode_bench_connector.py`, passes on this branch** (verified by checking out main's connector and re-running).
- `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_decode_bench_connector.py -q` → 30/30 pass.
- E2E on the Reproduction setup (single node, TP8 + MultiConnector): on v0.32.0 as released, the first request with ISL > 4096 asserts as above; with the fill-side fix in this branch, the same serving setup handles such requests normally.

AI assistance was used (analysis, fix, tests, validation); every changed line reviewed and tested by the submitter.

## Overview

Document the B300 MiniMax-M3.1-Flash AgentX lane of [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4467](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4467) (head `615ee422`, lane `minimaxm31flash-fp4-b300-vllm-agentic-dspark`) as two opt-in B300 presets in `recipes/models/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.yaml`. The lane runs one aggregated vLLM engine on a single 8-GPU B300 node with image `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m31-flash@sha256:86f582dae25ea92802353727164ae4eb03b37b18baf9119b805ffaec2a7ef07c` (vLLM `0.1.dev23341+g8744dd2fb` in the run logs). The recipe has no B300 preset yet, and no open PR covers this lane.

## Claims

Both presets use the default checkpoint, `single_node_tp`, text only (`--language-model-only`), the recipe's Blackwell NVFP4 KV/indexer settings and seven-token DSpark draft, plus the lane's shared settings: `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`, `--stream-interval 20`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` with an explicit `cudagraph_capture_sizes` list up to 8192, `VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=600` and `VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_RENDER_TIMEOUT=600`.

**`b300_agentx_tp4` (AgentX TP4, opt-in):** TP4, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`, DSpark draft attention on `FLASH_ATTN` (as qualified; the recipe's NVIDIA default stays `FLASHINFER_TS`). Nine points:

- GPU-resident KV: concurrency 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 with `--max-num-seqs` 2 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 64.
- Host-DRAM KV offload (the **Simple** KV-offload option, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, `kv_both`, `lazy_offload: true`, `cpu_bytes_to_use: 1499000000000` for the whole engine): concurrency 24 / 40 / 48 / 56 with `--max-num-seqs` 48 / 64 / 64 / 96.

**`b300_agentx_tp2` (AgentX TP2 + KV offload, opt-in):** TP2, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, DSpark draft attention on the recipe's `FLASHINFER_TS`, Simple KV offload with `cpu_bytes_to_use: 749000000000` and `lazy_offload: true` at every point. Concurrency 24 / 32 / 40 / 48 with `--max-num-seqs` 48 / 48 / 60 / 72.

Each preset has a runbook covering host-memory sizing (each rank pins about 349 GiB), the FLASH_ATTN/FLASHINFER_TS split, and the synthetic acceptance the benchmark used. `meta.date_updated` is bumped to 2026-10-27.

## Validation

- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <this checkout>/recipes` passes (vllm-project/recipes @ `5790dff`): 217 recipes, JSON API built.
- I built the full JSON API before and after the change. Only MiniMax-M3.1-Flash files change: `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.json` and its promoted variant `amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4.json` (each gains `presets` and the new `date_updated`), and `presets/b300_agentx_tp4.json` and `presets/b300_agentx_tp2.json` are added. The B300 baseline rendering does not change, because both presets are opt-in.
- All 13 rendered points match the lane's effective arguments and environment at the PR head (`agentic.yaml` base merged with each point's override) once the exclusions below are removed.
- The rendered TP4 c24 and TP2 c24 commands also match the `vllm serve` commands logged in run [40340506758](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/40340506758) (attempt 3), except for the synthetic acceptance settings. In both server logs the connector comes from `--kv-transfer-config` (`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector: ... per_rank=349.01 GB, world_size=4, mode=lazy` and `per_rank=348.78 GB, world_size=2`), confirming that `cpu_bytes_to_use` is the budget for the whole engine. The logs also show `FLASH_ATTN` on TP4 and `FLASHINFER_TS` on TP2.

## Details

The schema expresses every serving setting of the lane. TP comes from the preset's `tp`; the host-DRAM tier comes from `select.kv_offload: simple`, with `json_args` on its `--kv-transfer-config` that swap the Simple option's per-rank default (`cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank`) for the lane's engine-wide `cpu_bytes_to_use`, the same pattern as MiniMax-M3's `b200_agentx`. The capture list and the TP4 draft backend are `json_args` edits as well. The lane ran one engine per node; running several TP2 engines on one node is not qualified, and each engine would need its own share of host RAM (noted in the runbook).

Excluded as InferenceX-only or no-op:

- **Benchmark-only settings:** concurrency lists, synthetic acceptance (`rejection_sample_method: synthetic`, `synthetic_acceptance_length: 4.04`, injected by the benchmark; the presets keep block verification), AIPerf settings, `dram-utilization`.
- **Harness plumbing:** `--served-model-name` and the local `/model` path, `--host`/`--port`, `--device-ids` (GPU placement), `--disable-uvicorn-access-log`, `PYTHONUNBUFFERED`, `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` (the lane is single-engine, with no data-parallel engine wait).
- **Defaults:** `--max-model-len 1048576` equals the checkpoint's `max_position_embeddings`, and the logs report 1,048,576 tokens per request. `--trust-remote-code` is not needed because vLLM registers the `minimax_m3_vl` config itself (`vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`), and the recipe's existing B300 commands, on the same image tag, omit it.
- **`VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD`:** a no-op here (the lane sets `1` on its offload points and `0` on the resident ones). vLLM reads it only in `VllmConfig._post_init_kv_transfer_config`, to choose the connector when `--kv-offloading-size` is set (`vllm/config/vllm.py` on `main`). The lane never sets `--kv-offloading-size` (absent from the logged non-default args) and passes the connector explicitly. The pinned build's commit `8744dd2fb` is not in this repository, so this is checked against `main` and against the logged connector creation.

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Read only a group's own regions in hybrid SSM transfers
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

In the NIXL hybrid (attention + SSM) descriptor path, every attention group read **all** registered regions. When some regions hold only another group's layers, every attention block re-reads those bytes, which that group's own descriptors already transfer. On GLM-5.3-Flash this made ~38% of the wire bytes duplicates.

`register_kv_caches` now records which transfer groups have layers in each region. `_compute_desc_ids` addresses only a group's own regions, for both attention and SSM groups. This generalizes the existing `CircularBufferSpec` special case (`_scratch_region_indices`, removed). The wire format is unchanged. See the example at the bottom.

## Results

P TP2 → D TP2 on separate GB300 nodes, pull mode, fp8 KV, scrambled KV pool, 2 runs per point.

| Model | ISL | Bytes / req (before → after) | Descs | Xfer avg | GSM8K via P/D (before → after) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3-Flash | 32k | 859,615,744 → 565,391,872 (−34%) | 950 → 646 | ~8.4 → ~5.2 ms | |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | 100k | 2,177,711,104 → 1,348,099,072 (−38%) | 2150 → 1306 | ~20.5 → ~12.4 ms | 81.8% → 80.6% (run-to-run 80.8–82.8%) |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B | 32k / 100k | identical | identical | | 40.8% → 41.2% (non-P/D 41.2%) |

- **Byte model:** a byte-level model of the descriptor layout reproduces every pre-fix measurement exactly (9 points). The 283,136 B left above the useful bytes is the tail page aliasing an indexer region and being read at the indexer's block length. That is region identity (base-address keying), which #57662 fixes, so it is out of scope here.
- **Unaffected layouts:** layouts where every group has a layer in every region (pure attention, non-SSM models through the fast path, Qwen3.5/Nemotron-style hybrids) produce the same descriptor ids as before.

## Tests

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_tp_mapping.py
# PR (f1a5bab606):   557 passed, 4 failed, 113 errors
# main (be03d19750): 555 passed, 4 failed, 113 errors   <- identical failing set
```

- **Same failures on main:** the failing tests are exactly the same on unpatched main. They are test-environment issues: the `test_nixl_connector.py` fixtures error at setup with a venv prebuilt from an older commit, HF is offline, and the FlashMLA module is missing. None of them touch region selection.
- **New:** `test_mla_hybrid_groups_read_only_their_own_regions[False/True]`. `[True]` adds a KDA-only tensor and fails without the `base_worker.py` change. `[False]` (every group in every region) passes before and after.
- **Existing tests:** `_scratch_region_indices` assertions now check `_group_region_indices[<scratch group>]`, with the same values.
- `pre-commit` passes.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Remote descriptor ids use the local group→region map.** This adds no new assumption. The hybrid path already builds remote ids from local `_ssm_region_indices`, `_ple_group_index` and `_scratch_region_indices`, and the handshake asserts identical per-region block lengths for hybrid MLA+SSM. If P and D group layers differently, per-group `block_ids` would already disagree.
- **SSM descriptor layout:** each SSM layer owns `ssm_regions_per_layer` consecutive descriptors, in `_ssm_region_indices` order. The layout is unchanged; only the subset of slots read changes.
- **Not a duplicate:** no open PR fixes this. #57662 is complementary: it keys regions by `(base_addr, block_len)`, i.e. what a region *is*, while this PR fixes which groups *own* it. Both touch the same lines in `register_kv_caches`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to develop this change and write this description. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and e2e validation above.

## Example: what main does at runtime

This is the layout of the new unit test (`kda_only_tensor=True`): one MLA group M and two KDA groups Ka and Kb, where Ka has one extra layer. There are 4 blocks per region, all drawn from one shared pool, so each block id belongs to exactly one group.

**1. `register_kv_caches`** keys regions by base address:

| Region | Tensor | Layers in it | `region_group_ids` |
|---|---|---|---|
| r0 | tensor0 | mla.0, kda_a.0, kda_b.0 | -1 (shared) |
| r1 | tensor1 | mla.1, kda_a.1, kda_b.1 | -1 (shared) |
| r2 | tensor2 | kda_a.2 | 1 (Ka) |

`_ssm_region_indices = [0, 1, 2]`. The hybrid path never consults `region_group_ids`.

**2. Local descriptor list:** one handle holding two views of the same tensors.
- FA descriptors are `d = r*4 + block`, giving d0–d11.
- SSM descriptors are `d = 12 + (slot*4 + k)*4 + block`, giving d12–d59 (4 sub-descriptors per layer).

**3. A request with `block_ids = ([1], [2], [3])`** takes the hybrid path in `_compute_desc_ids`:

| Group | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| M | `arange(num_regions)` → d1, d5, **d9** | d1, d5 |
| Ka | `arange(num_ssm_regions)` → slots r0, r1, r2 | slots r0, r1, r2 |
| Kb | `arange(num_ssm_regions)` → slots r0, r1, **r2** | slots r0, r1 |

- **d9** is tensor2 at block 1. Block 1 belongs to M, but M has no layer in tensor2.
- **Kb's r2 slot** is tensor2 at block 3. Block 3 belongs to Kb, but Kb has no layer in tensor2.

No layer ever writes those pages. Reading them doesn't corrupt anything, but every byte is wasted.

**On GLM-5.3-Flash** (11 DSA, 34 KDA in 4 groups, 11 `KPOOL_TAIL` layers; 40 regions per rank):
- The d9 case is every DSA block re-reading the 8 KDA-only regions (2.2 MB each) and the 10 tail-only regions (2 KB each).
- The Kb case is the two 8-layer KDA groups each reading one empty slot.

At 100k that is 829,612,032 of the 829,895,168 duplicate bytes measured. The remaining 283,136 B are the #57662 aliasing case.

## Purpose

Follow-up to #58211, where the (DGX) Spark GPQA eval has been failing with `RuntimeError: Server exited unexpectedly` across several nightlies.

`gpt-oss-20b-sm120.yaml` is the only config in `tests/evals/gpt_oss/configs/` with no `server_args`, so the engine falls back to the default `gpu_memory_utilization` of 0.92. Spark's GPU memory is unified with system RAM, and free memory on the CI Spark varies by a few GiB around that 0.92 request (111.95 GiB), so the startup check can refuse to allocate, EngineCore exits, and the harness only surfaces its own terse message. The MI355 GPQA step mirrors the Spark step and runs the same `models-spark.txt`, so it picks up 0.6 too (fine for a 20B model).

## Test Plan

Run the eval exactly as CI does, on a DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64, CUDA 13.0, sm_121), against a source build of `main`:

```
pytest tests/evals/gpt_oss/test_gpqa_correctness.py --config-list-file=configs/models-spark.txt
```

## Test Result

Before (on my Spark, which had 83.35 GiB free at the time):

```
INFO [model.py:2097] Using max model len 131072
(EngineCore) ValueError: Free memory on device cuda:0 (83.35/121.7 GiB) on startup is less than
  desired GPU memory utilization (0.92, 111.96 GiB).
(EngineCore) EngineCore failed to start.
E   RuntimeError: Server exited unexpectedly.        # tests/utils.py:706
```

After:

```
(EngineCore) Available KV cache memory: 57.69 GiB
(EngineCore) GPU KV cache size: 2,395,438 tokens, Maximum concurrency for 131,072 tokens per request: 18.28x
(APIServer) INFO:     Application startup complete.
```

Server comes up, and 57 GiB of KV cache is far more than this eval needs.

I can't run the GPQA body itself here — my box is missing the `gpt_oss` eval package — so this is verified up to server startup, not to the accuracy number. And I can't read the Buildkite logs, so if the Spark job output does *not* contain `Free memory on device cuda:0`, something else is going on and this should be closed.

0.6 is a conservative pick rather than a tuned one; happy to change it if you'd prefer a different value.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][Attention] Keep the bf16 attention prefill when FP8 padding would double the heads
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
The gfx950 FP8 asm MLA prefill needs 16-aligned heads, so smaller per-rank head counts are padded up to 16. At 8 heads per rank (Kimi-K2.x at TP8) that doubles the kernel's work, and the asm kernel plus its split-tile reduce end up ~2x slower per layer than the bf16 flash-attention prefill. This PR adds `AiterMLAHelper.is_valid_fp8_prefill_num_heads`, which rejects head counts that padding would at least double (1-8 per rank), and uses it in the two places that enable the FP8 prefill. Those counts go back to bf16 flash attention; 9-15 (e.g. Kimi-K3 at TP8, 12 heads) and 16+ are unchanged. Decode still uses `is_valid_num_heads`, so nothing changes there.

#51040 extended the FP8 prefill to smaller head counts for Kimi-K3, whose ranks hold 12 heads at TP8. Its new gate reused the decode head-count predicate, which also accepts counts that divide 16, so Kimi-K2.x at TP8 (8 heads per rank) moved onto the padded FP8 path as a side effect, on a shape the change wasn't tuned or measured for. For Kimi-K2.x at TP8 this PR restores the earlier prefill path:


| | FP8 prefill gate | Kimi-K2.6 TP8 prefill (8 heads/rank) |
|---|---|---|
| Before #51040 | `num_heads % 16 == 0` | bf16 flash attention |
| After #51040 (current main) | `is_valid_num_heads` (pads up to 16) | FP8 asm, padded 8 → 16 heads |
| This PR | `is_valid_fp8_prefill_num_heads` | bf16 flash attention |

## Claims
- Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4 TP8 on MI355X, current main (including #59634's fused q/k/v prep): prefill attention 442 → 213 µs per layer, −14.0 ms on a 31,745-token prefill step and −25.1 ms on a single 1,024-token prefill; mean TTFT −7.9%.
- Only per-rank head counts of 1-8 change; decode is untouched.

## Why the FP8 path is slower at 8 heads per rank
Per-layer prefill attention on the 31,745 prompt tokens + 32 decode rows step, rank-0 kernel sums from the torch profiler:

| Step | FP8 asm path (main) | bf16 path (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| q/k/v prep | 76.9 µs (`_fused_mla_prefill_qkv_fp8`: k concat, pad 8 → 16 heads, fp8 cast) | 87.4 µs (k concat and copies) |
| Attention kernel | 170.0 µs (`mla_pfl_qh192_vh128_m32x8_n128x1_causal1`, 16 heads; half the output is padding) | 125.1 µs (`gqa_d192_v128_kernel`, 8 heads) |
| Split-tile reduce | 164.0 µs (`kn_mla_reduce_v1_ps<128,16,1>`) | — |
| Copies | 30.8 µs | — |
| **Total per layer** | **441.7 µs** | **212.5 µs** |

#59634 cut the prep cost (previously ~560 µs of padding copies and casts), but the asm kernel at twice the heads plus its reduce still cost more than flash attention on its own. The reduce's cost also depends heavily on the batch shape:

| Prefill step | Reduce, per layer | bf16 attention path | FP8 attention path | Saved by this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,024 tokens, 1 request | 425 µs | 3.4 ms | 28.4 ms | 25.1 ms |
| 32,767 + 1 | 4 µs | 13.4 ms | 17.2 ms | 3.8 ms |
| 31,745 + 32 | 164 µs | 13.0 ms | 27.0 ms | 14.0 ms |

## Validation
Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4, TP8, MI355X, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` (the backend resolves to `ROCM_AITER_MLA` with or without `--attention-backend`). This branch rebased on main, so the two runs differ only in Python files. `vllm bench serve`, random 1024/1024, concurrency 64, `--ignore-eos --temperature 0 --request-rate inf`.

| Metric | main (FP8 asm prefill) | This PR (bf16 prefill) |
|---|---|---|
| Mean TTFT, 256 prompts, no profiler | 849.01 ms | 782.15 ms (−7.9%) |
| Median TTFT, 256 prompts, no profiler | 636.54 ms | 614.13 ms (−3.5%) |
| P99 TTFT, 256 prompts, no profiler | 1,165.51 ms | 1,116.27 ms (−4.2%) |
| Mean TTFT, 64 prompts, profiled run | 952.50 ms | 914.19 ms (−4.0%) |

TPOT and E2EL are left out on purpose: on current main the FP8 run produces wrong output (see the note below), which changes MoE routing during decode, so its decode timings aren't comparable.

GSM8K 5-shot, flexible / strict:

| main (FP8 asm prefill) | This PR (bf16 prefill) |
|---|---|
| 0.0281 / 0.0235 | 0.9439 / 0.9431 |

Tests: `pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_head_padding.py tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py` on MI355X: <fill in>. The new `test_fp8_prefill_rejects_head_counts_padding_doubles` needs no GPU; it checks that 1-8 heads are rejected for FP8 prefill but still valid for decode, and that 9, 12, 15, 16, 24, 32, 64, 128 and 144 keep FP8 prefill.

## Note on accuracy on current main
Separately from performance, FP8 prefill output on current main is wrong for 8 heads per rank. #59634's fused prep pads heads by tiling (padded head h = real head h % 8), while `_mla_fp8_prefill_attn` unpads divisor counts at stride `nhead // num_heads`, which matches `repeat_interleave` padding. Only head 0 ends up in the right place, hence the GSM8K score above. Before #59634, with the unpad fix in place, the FP8 path scored 0.9333 / 0.9333, so the performance argument above doesn't depend on the bug. This PR keeps 8 heads off that path but does not change the unpad itself, which is still inconsistent with the fused prep for head counts that divide 16. On main, Kimi-K2.x TP8 users can currently avoid it only by changing the KV cache dtype or the decode backend.

## Details
`is_valid_num_heads` itself is not changed because `check_num_heads_validity` asserts it in the `AiterMLAImpl` constructor and in the sparse MLA backend; rejecting 8 heads there would refuse to start the backend instead of falling back. The new predicate is a prefill-only check on top of it. Head counts of 1-7 per rank were not measured; padding costs them at least 2x the work as well, and they were also on bf16 prefill before #51040.

No duplicate: no open issue or PR changes the FP8 MLA prefill head-count gate. #59124 (open) adds a separate opt-in FlyDSL FP8 prefill.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change and description; I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][aiter] officially supporting aiter Triton kernels+dsv4 on RDNA3

## Purpose

Enable the AITER Triton FP8 paths on **RDNA3**, bringing it to parity with the gfx12/RDNA4 enablement. This also completes full GPU kernel support for **dsv4** models.
## Major Changes
* enable AITER unified attention if `VLLM_USE_AITER`=1. the priority is after `ROCM_ATTN` and before `TRITON_ATTN`.
* enable AITER GDN kernel.
* Widen most gates to all of RDNA which were only for RDNA4.

**Relationship to prior work:**

- **Continuation / mirror of #43615**. This PR
extends the exact same mechanism to gfx11/RDNA3 — both are RDNA, neither has a CK build, so only aiter's Triton kernels exist on either. Instead of duplicating the gate for a third arch, it switches the two RDNA gates to the canonical `on_rdna()` predicate (`gfx11 + gfx12`, minus CDNA gfx1250), so every downstream site (fp8 MoE oracles, blockscale linear, quant-fusion passes, pass-manager, GDN, sparse-MLA) lights up for gfx11 with no per-site edits.

- **Supplement to #47017**. That PR made DSV4
*run* on gfx11 but relied on the op-level **CPU/torch
fallback**, without broadly enabling AITER. The usage of "item()" from PyTorch fail cudagraph capture and can only be used with --enforce-eager". 
This PR removes that torch-fallback dependence for gfx11 by registering **all** aiter ops through the general path and
partially reverted the fragile _direct_register_custom_op_() for single kernel.

- **Supersedes #51555** . It adds a *separate* kernel that dequantizes fp8 → bf16 **in-kernel** before `tl.dot`, when the Triton compiler already implicitly does the same work during lowering, after minor fix https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4764. Simply adapting the Aiter's kernel is cleaner.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: opt-in dense weight cache for RDNA hybrid prefill
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds opt-in `KernelConfig.rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant` (`"enable"`/`"disable"`, case-insensitive, default `"disable"`). When it is `"enable"`, `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` caches a dense fp16/bf16 copy of each weight at load time and runs GEMMs with `M >= 256` on it, so prefill no longer dequantizes int4.

## Claims

- TTFT −22% to −26% on Qwen3-4B/8B w4a16 and −21% on Gemma-4-31B AWQ with MTP-3, on Strix
  Halo (gfx1151). TPOT is unchanged at concurrency 1.
- No accuracy change: GSM8K is within ±0.6 pp.
- Decode, small batches and spec-decode verify stay on the int4 path.
- Disabled by default, which leaves current behaviour unchanged.

## Validation

Usage: `--kernel-config '{"rdna_hybrid_w4a16_prefill_dequant": "enable"}'`. `vllm bench serve` with random 2048 in, concurrency 1, `disable` vs `enable` on the same build, interleaved (3 pairs per Qwen model, 2 for Gemma); values are the mean of per-run medians. Measured only on gfx1151; the kernel also runs on other gfx11/gfx12 parts, where the `M >= 256` threshold may need tuning.

| Model | TTFT disable → enable | TPOT disable → enable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RedHatAI Qwen3-8B w4a16, fp16 (asym) | 1328 → 1033 ms (**−22.2%**) | 27.7 → 27.7 ms |
| RedHatAI Qwen3-8B w4a16, bf16 (asym) | 1341 → 1023 ms (**−23.7%**) | 28.2 → 28.2 ms |
| RedHatAI Qwen3-4B w4a16, fp16 (sym) | 782 → 578 ms (**−26.1%**) | 16.4 → 16.5 ms |
| cyankiwi Gemma-4-31B AWQ, MTP-3, 128 out | 8.75 → 6.88 s (**−21.4%**) | 68.0 → 67.2 ms |

Disabled matches current main (554340f3d3) within 1% TTFT on all four models.

At concurrency 16 (Qwen3-8B fp16, 512 in / 256 out, 64 prompts, 2 pairs): TTFT 3069 → 2252 ms (−26.6%), TPOT 85.2 → 83.1 ms.

GSM8K (in-tree `tests/evals/gsm8k`, 5-shot, 500 questions, concurrency 16), Qwen3-8B: fp16 0.886 → 0.880, bf16 0.872 → 0.878.

`pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py`: All 293 passed on gfx1151.

## Details

- **Why opt-in:** the copy is 4x the int4 layer weight and is taken from the `gpu_memory_utilization` budget, so it comes out of KV cache. Qwen3-8B: +13.5 GiB weights, −13.5 GiB KV. Gemma-4-31B: weights 20.2 → 75.1 GiB, KV 71.6 → 16.6 GiB. The trade targets unified-memory parts like Strix Halo, where TTFT matters more than KV capacity. Enabling it caches every layer or none: if the copies do not fit while leaving 4 GiB of activation headroom plus KV cache for one `max_model_len` request, startup fails with an error naming the option. It is a mode string rather than a bool so further modes can be added without renaming it.
- **Why `M >= 256`:** below it the dense GEMM is still memory bound and reads 4x the bytes. Per-GEMM on gfx1151 it is up to 2.3x slower than int4 on Gemma-4-31B MLP shapes. At 256 and above it is no slower on any Qwen3-8B or Gemma-4-31B shape measured.
- **Limitation:** the dense copy is built once at load time, so in-place weight reloads (`reload_weights`, RL weight sync through the weight-transfer engines) are not supported with `"enable"`. The option is intended for pure inference; keep it `"disable"` when weights are updated at runtime.

### Related Work
- no open PR caches a dense copy of W4A16 weights for this kernel.
- #55711 makes the int4 prefill dequant cheaper, and this PR skips it, so the two stack. On top of #55711 this PR still cut TTFT by 6.7% (Qwen3-8B fp16), 12.8% (Qwen3-4B fp16) and 23.0% (Qwen3-8B bf16, since #55711 is fp16 only)
- #52637 (int4 repack in `process_weights_after_loading`) and #55742 (profiler labels) touch the same file, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.
- #53709 applies the same idea (opt-in load-time dequant for prefill) to DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 experts on another GPU family. It's a different kernel with no shared code path.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][Kimi-K3] Fold q_b_proj and W_UK into one GEMM for the MLA decode query
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On the ROCm/AITER decode path every Kimi-K3 MLA layer spends two launches on the query
projection (M = 56 rows at the InferenceX c14 point, 12 heads per rank at TP8):

| Kernel | What it does | Before (µs) | After (µs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hgemm_bf16_t16x32x128x5` | `q_b_proj`: x[56,1536] → q[56,12,192] | 6.76 | – |
| `_batched_gemm_a16wfp4_kernel` | absorb-in BMM: q_nope × W_UK (fp4) → ql_nope[56,12,512] | 5.49 | – |
| `_gemm_a16_w16_kernel` (aiter Triton `gemm_a16w16`) | x[56,1536] × W_fold[1536,6912] → [ql_nope \| q_pe] | – | 9.20 |
| **per layer** |  | **12.25** | **9.20** |

`q_b_proj` and the `W_UK` are consecutive linear maps, so
`ql_nope[h] = x · (W_UK[h] · W_qb_nope[h])ᵀ`. This PR builds once at load, from the bf16
checkpoint weights,

    W_fold[h] = [ W_UK[h] · W_qb_nope[h] ; W_qb_pe[h] ]        # [512 + 64, 1536] per head


**Decode only:** the W_UK absorb exists only on the MQA decode path. Prefill uses the
un-absorbed form and keeps `q_b_proj`, so any step with prefill tokens takes the original path.

**Small M win:** the fold reads 21 MB instead of 7.5 MB and does 2.5x the FLOPs. The save shrinks as M grows and would turn negative at prefill sizes, which this path never sees. 

We do additional 1.9Gb for the extra weight fold for all 93 layers of Kimi k3.

We're actively testing the prefill shape such that it cannot be much worse than non w-fold so that we don't have to pay for extra 1.9Gb.

## Server command:
```
export VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=7200 PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1200
export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=0 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER=0 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_KV_GATHER=0
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 PYTHONHASHSEED=42 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
# InferenceX agentic.yaml c14 point (vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-36768d1bf, 8x MI355X)
vllm serve /data/Kimi-K3 --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8002 \
  --trust-remote-code --moe-backend auto --tensor-parallel-size 8 --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --language-model-only --max-num-seqs 28 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --max-model-len 1048576 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL","max_cudagraph_capture_size":112,"custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"],"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[2,3,...,112]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":224875000000,"lazy_offload":false}}'
```

## Bench Command:
```
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --tokenizer /data/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code \
  --host localhost --port 8002 --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --request-rate=inf --random-prefix-len 0 --num-prompts 140 --max-concurrency 14 --ignore-eos --seed 43 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

## Test Results

**Conc 14** (InferenceX c14, DSpark k=3, 140 prompts)

| Metric | Before | After | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 685.62 | 693.13 | +1.1% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 19.47 | 19.27 | -1.0% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 340.08 | 336.53 | -1.0% |

**Conc 48** (InferenceX c48, no draft model, DCP 8, 480 prompts)

| Metric | Before | After | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|

## Purpose

The dense-MLA prefill spends four kernels per context chunk in
`_compute_prefill_context`:
- `vllm::gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache<bf16,bf16,(0),576,64>`
