commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSV4.1][Perf] Single-launch DSA decode candidate mask
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm, the DeepSeek V4.1 decode candidate mask goes from four kernels per consumer indexer layer to one. The flags kernel is folded into `_mask_candidates_strided_kernel` (added in [#56628](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56628)), and the int64 cast and `zeros_like` before it are dropped. No existing PR does this; [#57859](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57859) touches the same code, see Details.

## Claims

- The decode candidate mask is 1.06× to 2.50× faster on MI355X (not counting the two removed elementwise kernels, about 9.6 µs more per call).
- Mean TPOT -0.48% and throughput +0.44% end to end on MI355X, over 12 sweep points.
- Masking within `[0, end)` is unchanged, and GSM8K accuracy is unchanged within error.



## Validation



### Kernel

MI355X, CUDA graph (50 calls per replay, best of 5): width 262144, 2048 candidate blocks of 8, ends set to the live length. "Old" is `_candidate_flags_kernel` + `_mask_candidates_strided_kernel`. Every point matched the old output and the shared `apply_candidate_mask` exactly over `[0, end)`.


| rows | live cols | old µs | new µs | speedup |
| ---- | --------- | ------ | ------ | ------- |
| 4    | 2048      | 5.71   | 3.11   | 1.84×   |
| 16   | 2048      | 6.03   | 3.20   | 1.88×   |
| 64   | 2048      | 8.04   | 3.54   | 2.27×   |
| 256  | 2048      | 17.11  | 6.84   | 2.50×   |
| 4    | 15000     | 6.22   | 3.51   | 1.77×   |
| 64   | 15000     | 8.82   | 4.48   | 1.97×   |
| 256  | 15000     | 20.06  | 9.64   | 2.08×   |
| 16   | 32000     | 6.90   | 3.92   | 1.76×   |
| 64   | 32000     | 10.02  | 6.48   | 1.55×   |
| 256  | 32000     | 25.94  | 16.98  | 1.53×   |
| 16   | 131072    | 9.98   | 7.10   | 1.41×   |
| 64   | 131072    | 20.27  | 18.01  | 1.13×   |
| 256  | 131072    | 53.21  | 50.28  | 1.06×   |




### End-to-end

vLLM on MI355X, TP4 + EP, FP8, fused against default. Mean TPOT in ms and output throughput in tok/s:


| input / output | concurrency | TPOT default | TPOT fused | Δ     | tok/s default | tok/s fused | Δ     |
| -------------- | ----------- | ------------ | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | ----------- | ----- |
| 8192 / 1024    | 4           | 8.05         | 7.99       | -0.7% | 470.57        | 472.20      | +0.3% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 8           | 9.81         | 9.73       | -0.9% | 772.13        | 778.70      | +0.9% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 16          | 11.85        | 11.74      | -0.9% | 1262.90       | 1273.77     | +0.9% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 32          | 16.16        | 16.07      | -0.6% | 1783.04       | 1793.30     | +0.6% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 64          | 23.07        | 22.84      | -1.0% | 2523.76       | 2545.75     | +0.9% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 128         | 35.20        | 35.15      | -0.1% | 3176.89       | 3182.50     | +0.2% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 256         | 57.90        | 57.72      | -0.3% | 3814.25       | 3827.03     | +0.3% |
| 60000 / 600    | 4           | 14.05        | 13.97      | -0.6% | 227.76        | 229.03      | +0.6% |
| 60000 / 600    | 16          | 40.27        | 40.02      | -0.6% | 335.86        | 337.69      | +0.5% |
| 60000 / 600    | 64          | 137.05       | 137.15     | +0.1% | 391.59        | 391.60      | +0.0% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 4           | 16.74        | 16.68      | -0.4% | 185.73        | 186.21      | +0.3% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 16          | 53.98        | 54.17      | +0.3% | 248.75        | 248.60      | -0.1% |


The mean is -0.48% TPOT and +0.44% throughput. No single point moves by more than 1%, but throughput improves at 11 of the 12 and TPOT at 10, and median TPOT gives the same answer at -0.53%.



### Accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, via `lm_eval`:


| filter           | default         | fused           | Δ       |
| ---------------- | --------------- | --------------- | ------- |
| flexible-extract | 0.9227 ± 0.0074 | 0.9363 ± 0.0067 | +0.0136 |
| strict-match     | 0.9219 ± 0.0074 | 0.9371 ± 0.0067 | +0.0152 |


The fused path scores higher on both filters, by 1.4σ and 1.5σ against a combined standard error of about 0.010, so the difference is not significant.



### Tests

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_candidate_mask.py \
       tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py
```

Both pass on MI355X. `test_matches_shared_kernel_model_shape` is new and runs 2048 candidates, crowded and spread, at 8 and 64 rows so both tile sizes run. `test_matches_shared_kernel_candidates_past_width` is new and covers the last-column clamp. `test_leaves_columns_past_end_untouched` now asserts that nothing at or past `end` is written. The mxfp4 indexer tests cover the other caller of `_apply_candidate_mask_strided`. CI runs these in the MI300 attention-kernels job.

At the call site, the old and new sequences give bitwise-identical logits and candidates for the mask and select paths, with `next_n` of 1 and 2 and with 1-D and 2-D `seq_lens`. A profiler run shows the old mask path launched three kernels per call and the new one launches one.

## Details

Each consumer layer (4 per decode step) masked its decode logits with four kernels:


| kernel                            | source                                                               | µs per call |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `direct_copy`                     | `visible.to(torch.int64)`                                            | 4.4         |
| `FillFunctor<long>`               | `torch.zeros_like(visible)`                                          | 5.2         |
| `_candidate_flags_kernel`         | clears all `nblocks + 1` flags per row, then scatters the candidates | 8.7         |
| `_mask_candidates_strided_kernel` | masks `[0, end)` from the flags                                      | 4.1         |


The flags kernel clears the whole row, however short the live context. The two elementwise kernels only build an all-zero starts tensor and an int64 copy of `seq_lens`, and the Triton kernels need neither.

`_mask_candidates_strided_kernel` now builds its own flags. Each row's tiles are handed out round-robin to its programs, and each program clears the flags of its own live tiles, scatters the candidates that land in them, and masks. Nothing past the live context is cleared. On AMD, `tl.debug_barrier()` only waits for LDS traffic, so a store wait goes before each barrier and the flags are read with `.cv`. The wait is `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)` on gfx9, `s_waitcnt_vscnt` on gfx11 and `s_wait_storecnt` on gfx12, since gfx10+ count stores separately. The tile is 2048 columns below 64 rows and 4096 from 64 rows up. It depends only on the row count, so the grid stays fixed under FULL CUDA graphs. Stores now stop at `end` instead of the next 1024-column boundary.

At the decode call site, the int64 cast, `zeros_like` and `repeat_interleave` are replaced by `None` starts, the int32 `seq_lens` and `row_repeat`, as on the CUDA path. This applies to both the mask and the select paths.

**Limitations.** The tile sizes were tuned on gfx950 only. gfx942 runs in CI but was not benchmarked. The gfx11 and gfx12 store waits were checked in the compiled ISA only, since no RDNA hardware was available.

## Existing PRs and interaction with #57859

I searched vllm-project/vllm PRs (open and closed) for the kernel names, "candidate flags / mask / fuse", `zeros_like` and `row_repeat` with ROCm. No PR fuses the flags and mask kernels or removes these two elementwise kernels. [#56628](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56628) (merged) added the strided decode mask that this PR builds on and kept the separate flags kernel. [#57859](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57859) (open) adds a candidate-only paged MQA scorer for gfx950 decode and edits the same code.

- **Its fast path skips the mask.** On gfx950, consumer layers with `compress_ratio == 1`, `next_n == 1`, no `requires_padding` and a page size that is a multiple of the candidate block size score only the candidate columns. Top-k then runs on the compact buffer, so no mask kernel runs. In that case, which probably covers the four V4.1 consumer layers in decode without speculative decoding, this PR's fused kernel doesn't run.
- **Its dense fallback still has what this PR changes.** The fallback keeps `repeat_interleave`, `.to(torch.int64)`, `zeros_like`, then select or mask. It is used by:
  - the candidate source layer, which always takes this path because the fast path requires `candidate_write` to be false, so removing the cast and zero-fill still saves two kernels per step there;
  - gfx942, `next_n > 1`, padded decode and `compress_ratio != 1`;
  - `rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py`, which calls the strided mask directly.
- **As posted, #57859 reverts code on** `main`**.** Its diff deletes `_mask_candidates_strided_kernel` and `_apply_candidate_mask_strided` (from #56628), so its fallback goes back to the shared full-width `_apply_candidate_mask`. It also deletes the C4A Triton paged-MQA decode path, the native top-512 gate in `_get_aiter_top_k_kernel` and `FP8_DTYPE`. `rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py` still imports `_apply_candidate_mask_strided`, so merging as-is would break that import. This is most likely a stale branch (last updated 2026-09-23) and needs a rebase.
- **Merge order.**
  - If this PR lands first, #57859's rebase should keep `_apply_candidate_mask_strided` in its fallback and adopt the `None` starts and `row_repeat` call. The conflict is in the same `if candidate_blocks is not None:` block.
  - If #57859 lands first, this change moves into its `else:` branch.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix `vllm bench forward` on hybrid attention/recurrent models: initialize packed KV caches using manager-block views and reserve/restore all speculative recurrent state slots.

## Claims

- Packed hybrid KV layouts no longer fail with `No block dim of size ...` during benchmark initialization.
- Verify requests get disjoint recurrent scratch blocks for every configured speculative token, and replay restores all those blocks.
- Changes are confined to benchmark setup and replay state; serving execution and the timed model-forward interval are unchanged.

## Validation

GB200 validation of the retained tests: 3 cases passed (native CLI, cache isolation, recurrent state). All targeted pre-commit checks pass.

Base: `b82393b77315692f390880d2e931fdc1fbd13928`. Validation used four GB200 GPUs, native MRV2, and dummy weights (this checks benchmark execution/state, not model accuracy).

| Reproducer | Base | Fixed |
|---|---|---|
| Native GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, FP8 KV, FlashInfer sparse MLA, ngram 5 target-only | All ranks fail: `ValueError: No block dim of size 3979 in (6619401, 64, 132)` | Decode, Verify, Mixed finish; all ranks finite, deterministic, graph/eager relative RMS 0 |
| Tiny Qwen3Next public CLI | `assert 5 == (1 + (7 * 2))` fails: only one state per request | Passes: all speculative slots counted, Verify/Mixed finite and deterministic |
| CPU speculative-state regression | Too few recurrent scratch slots per request | Passes capacity, non-overlap, and complete state-restoration checks |
| CPU packed-view regression | Native GLM reproducer above covers the original layout failure | Passes; adjacent interleaved layers remain unchanged |

Native cases: `decode=1*1@512`, `verify=2*6@512:5`, `mixed=128@512,2*6@512:5`; two samples of two replays. Measured medians were 4.723 / 8.443 / 20.134 ms respectively, with sample spreads 0.04% / 0.03% / 0.05%. These are execution checks, not a speedup claim.

Commands (run from this checkout with the installed vLLM environment):

```bash
/home/woosuk/workspace/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py -k 'test_bench_packed_kv_blocks or test_bench_speculative_mamba_blocks or test_bench_forward_hybrid_verify' -v
```

Final CPU selection: 7 passed; public CLI: 1 passed (53.47 s), base: 1 failed (52.53 s).

The public CLI regression creates a local tiny Qwen3Next model and checks finite, deterministic Verify/Mixed replay. The benchmark instantiates the real LLM engine. No checkpoint loading behavior changes; dummy weights are appropriate to this forward-state regression.

## Details

Hybrid cache groups can pack multiple attention kernel blocks inside one manager block and interleave layers. The existing `AttentionGroup.map_kv_cache_to_manager_blocks` reconstructs the correct manager view without copying. Recurrent state requires one base slot plus `MambaSpec.num_speculative_blocks`; unlike attention tails, every recurrent slot may be read or overwritten during verification.

These three fixes form one benchmark-state correctness change: without the packed-view fix the affected hybrid model cannot initialize; without either recurrent-state fix verification allocates or restores the wrong state. The CPU tests check allocation capacity and memory isolation without pinning block IDs or a complete storage layout. The snapshots use additional GPU memory proportional to the actual speculative state slots. Their copies remain outside the measured interval.

Duplicate-work checks searched open PRs for `"bench forward" "KV"`, `"bench forward" "Mamba"`, `"bench forward" "KDA"`, and `"packed" "benchmark"`. No open PR addressed these benchmark-state failures. The issue inventory came from local model experiments and has no linked GitHub issue number. Existing packed-cache connector and kernel PRs affect different paths.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to implement, test, and prepare this change. The human submitter confirmed review of every changed line and execution of the relevant tests before submission.
